React text escaping prevents a direct XSS from `labelHint`, but the data exposure itself is security/privacy relevant under the repository threat model's PII/waitlist data category.

title: Leaderboard pagination can amplify DB load
description: The leaderboard helper caps ranked rows with MAX_LEADERBOARD_USERS, but totalCount and totalPages are computed from the uncapped number of profiles with an email. Once totalCount exceeds the cap, hasMore remains true for pages that can never return rows because the ranked CTE only contains the first 2000 eligible profiles. The frontend introduced a while loop that keeps requesting pages until hasMore is false, and it repeats this on focus/visibility changes and every 30 seconds. Because each API request rebuilds point_totals by grouping the full points table, a public page view can trigger a large number of heavy DB aggregations, including many empty pages after the cap. An unauthenticated attacker can also call the public endpoint directly with arbitrary pages. This is an introduced availability risk against the API/database.

title: Hermit media replies bypass X posting authorization
description: The changed Hermit command path now derives mediaUrl from either Hermit attachments or any reply line that looks like an image URL, then sets shouldPostToXFirst to true whenever that mediaUrl exists. This applies to all Hermit kinds, not just the previously gated /gmeow path. AlfaClub Hermit commands are intentionally open to non-allowlisted room users, while the normal /x post command requires ADMIN/OWNER and --confirm. Because postTweetFromSystem directly calls the configured Twitter posting implementation, any AlfaClub room member who can cause /meme or /hermit to emit a .gif/.jpg/.png/.webp URL can make the application post to the configured X account. This creates an authorization bypass for public posts and can be abused for spam, phishing links, or reputational damage, bounded mainly by the existing one-post-per-minute group rate limit and the availability of configured X credentials.

title: Unauthenticated refresh bypass enables RPC scan DoS
description: The introduced migratedCoins API is a public GET endpoint. It maps the refresh query parameter directly to forceRefresh and passes it to fetchServerMigratedCoins without authentication or rate limiting. When forceRefresh is true, fetchServerMigratedCoins skips the cached result and also skips the inFlightScan single-flight guard, then starts a full migration scan from V4_LAUNCH_BLOCK using eth_getLogs over large historical ranges and additional eth_getCode trust checks. Concurrent requests with ?refresh=1 therefore create concurrent full-chain scans rather than sharing the existing in-flight scan. The scanner also backs off and sleeps on rate limits, which can tie up serverless execution while consuming RPC quota. A remote unauthenticated attacker can repeatedly request /api/zora/migratedCoins?refresh=1, or vary query strings to avoid edge cache reuse, to exhaust the configured Base logs RPC quota and degrade this API/app functionality.

title: Orchestrator API key exposed via process arguments
description: The commit adds scripts to deploy the Solana keeper orchestrator. The generated or reused SOLANA_ORCHESTRATOR_API_KEY is a bearer secret used by the orchestrator to authorize POST /reconcile requests. However, scripts/ops/remote-install-solana-orchestrator.sh passes this secret as a positional argument to the remote `bash -s` command and later interpolates it into a remote `curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer ...'` command. Command-line arguments are commonly visible through tools such as `ps` or `/proc/*/cmdline` to other local users, depending on host hardening. An unprivileged user on the admin workstation or Vultr host who observes the process during deployment can recover the orchestrator API key and then invoke keeper reconcile actions against the public orchestrator endpoint. The impact is limited by the orchestrator action allowlist and keeper-side idempotency, but it still exposes an operational secret that gates onchain keeper actions. The secret should be transmitted via stdin, a temporary root-only file, or an SSH channel that does not place it in argv; the health check should not include the bearer token, especially because /healthz does not require auth.

title: Terminal control-plane jobs can still execute
description: The commit replaced the keeper job runner's direct transition to running with beginOperationExecution. The old transitionOperationStatus call would throw on terminal states such as succeeded or cancelled because those states have no transition to running, preventing a stale or cancelled job from executing. The new helper instead returns { status: 'succeeded' | 'cancelled', resumedFromTerminal: false } without throwing. Because runOneJob ignores this result, it proceeds to callInternalApi anyway. A pending or retried keeper job that still references a terminal operation can therefore execute mutating keeper endpoints after the operation was completed or cancelled, bypassing the control-plane terminal-state guard. This is especially relevant because internal_api jobs may call /api/keeper/* endpoints that perform onchain keeper actions.

title: Control-plane operator endpoint bypasses zone auth
description: The commit adds the public route `/api/keeper/control-plane/operator-action`. The handler only calls `requireKeeprApiKey` before parsing an arbitrary operator action body and passing it to `executeOperatorAction`. That executor can perform onchain financial actions such as `vault.sweep`, `strategy.ajna.rebucket`, and `strategy.charm.rebalance`. Existing keeper action execution code treats these as trust-zone protected operations: it resolves the action's trust zone, looks up the zone-specific secret such as `KPR_ZONE_KEY_FINANCIAL_EXECUTION`, and requires the `x-keepr-zone-key` header when configured. The new endpoint does not perform that secondary authorization and also does not verify that the request is tied to a claimed control-plane job. As a result, any caller with the general KPR API key can directly invoke these operator actions and bypass the stronger financial-execution trust boundary intended for sensitive keeper writes.

title: Unbounded identity lookups can DoS AlfaClub digests
description: Both AlfaClub daily brief and radar now call readCreatorLabels(currentRows.map(...)) for the entire latest metrics snapshot. readCreatorLabels deduplicates the full list and then runs Promise.all over every unresolved address, performing Basename and then ENS lookups. Snapshot size is influenced by public onchain creator activity, while the digest only needs labels for top/mover/risk rows. An attacker who creates or causes many creator rows without cached chat usernames can force scheduled digest runs to open thousands of concurrent RPC requests, exhaust serverless resources, hit provider rate limits, or time out before sending/recording the digest.

title: Admin keeper tick can leak KPR key via Host header
description: The commit adds /api/admin/keeper/jobs/run, which lets an authenticated admin trigger runKeeperJobTick. If KEEPER_COORDINATION_BASE_URL is not configured, the handler builds baseUrl directly from req.headers.host and x-forwarded-proto. runKeeperJobTick later processes claimed internal_api jobs by POSTing to baseUrl + job.path with Authorization: Bearer <KPR_API_KEY>. A requester who can make an authenticated admin request with a spoofed Host header can redirect those server-side keeper calls to an attacker-controlled host and receive the KPR_API_KEY in the Authorization header. The KPR key protects keeper/automation endpoints that can perform protocol operations, so it should never be sent to a request-derived origin. This should be fixed by requiring a trusted configured coordination origin, deriving from a canonical server-side origin, or allowlisting the destination host before making KPR-authenticated internal requests.

title: CCA workflow bypasses canonical settlement gate
description: The new kpr/kpr-workflows/cca-finalization/main.ts delegates production workflow execution to executeCcaFinalization() from kpr/actions/cca-finalization.action.ts. That action explicitly documents that it is NON-CANONICAL, does not configure the hook fee plane, does not enforce completion invariants, and should only be used by manual/local non-canonical paths. It then directly calls sweepCurrency(), migrate(), and sweepUnsoldTokens(). The canonical /api/keeper/sweep handler performs the missing security-sensitive steps after migration: hook setTaxConfig-style fee-plane configuration and invariant checks covering fee recipient alignment, ShareOFT fee collector alignment, payout-router/burn-stream wiring, and treasury configuration. By making the workflow use the non-canonical direct action, migrated CCA vaults can remain without hook fee configuration or invariant enforcement, allowing post-migration trading/fee routing to operate in an unintended state until another process manually repairs it.

title: Zora handles can spoof X Ethos scores
description: The updated Zora explore Ethos resolution now selects `p.handle` as `zora_handle` and, when `twitter_username` is absent, uses that handle as the identifier for `service:x.com:username:<value>`. Zora handles and X usernames are different namespaces and should not be interchangeable. An attacker who controls a Zora profile/creator coin can choose a Zora handle matching a high-reputation X username and, if their profile lacks a real Twitter username, the API will fetch and apply the victim X account's Ethos score. The score is then used as the returned `ethosScore`, in sorting, and in the normal creator-list `ethosMin` filter, so users/API consumers can be misled into trusting or discovering a creator based on spoofed reputation.

title: AMOE relay falls back to generic keeper CSW credentials
description: The commit extends AMOE relay credential resolution beyond LOTTERY_AMOE_RELAY_* to KPR_ERC4337_* and KEEPR_ERC4337_* variables. If an operator configures generic keeper ERC-4337 credentials but intentionally leaves AMOE relay credentials unset, hasAmoeRelayConfig() can still return true and relayAmoeTransaction() will submit UserOperations through that generic keeper smart wallet. The AMOE submit endpoint is user-facing: after a valid signed AMOE proof and credit check, it builds a processAmoeEntry call and asks createAmoeRelay() to submit it. This does not appear to permit arbitrary calldata, but it breaks key/budget isolation and can cause lottery users to consume gas/paymaster allowance or nonce capacity from the main keeper wallet when AMOE was not explicitly provisioned. The existing regression test comments emphasize that AMOE should not inherit other service keys; these new KPR/KEEPR signer tuple fallbacks violate that isolation for the current keeper env names.

title: AMOE ZK UI burns credits before a non-retriable submit
description: This commit changes the AMOE entry card from the legacy single submit endpoint to a two-phase ZK flow. On a successful /burn-credits response, the client ignores the phase-A response metadata and immediately posts to /submit-zk. That is unsafe with the current submit-zk handler: it consumes the one-time nonce before checking the remaining AMOE balance in legacy mode and before checking burn-ledger snapshot availability in burn-then-submit mode. If phase A has just debited the user's balance, legacy-mode submit-zk can fail with insufficient_amoe_credits unless the user had at least twice the selected points. In burn-then-submit-required mode, immediate phase B can fail with amoe_burn_not_found or amoe_snapshot_not_yet_confirmed until publisher/snapshot state catches up. In both cases the nonce has already been consumed, so the same signed request cannot be retried, leaving the already debited credits orphaned until any refund cron eventually restores them and causing no lottery entry to be submitted.

title: AlfaClub proxy allows all /api/room endpoints
description: The Worker enforces allowed paths using a simple prefix check. This commit changes the deployed ALLOWED_PATH_PREFIXES value to include /api/room. Because isAllowedPath accepts any pathname equal to the prefix or below it, and the method gate allows GET, HEAD, OPTIONS, and POST, the Worker now forwards any /api/room/* request to the upstream AlfaClub API, not just POST /api/room/:roomId/message. The Worker is protected by x-proxy-secret, so this is not an unauthenticated open proxy. However, it weakens the intended route-level authorization boundary: anyone who obtains or is given the proxy secret can use the clean Worker egress path for unintended room APIs and arbitrary POST bodies/Authorization headers, bypassing the proxy’s documented endpoint minimization.

title: Deploy UI exposes role-policy bypass override
description: The new "Canary override" input accepts any integer from 0 to 65535 and includes it in both role-policy diagnostics and the deploy-session create payload. The server-side deploy-session code gives a request-supplied rolePolicyId precedence over creator/global defaults. That value is then used by the batcher's policy-aware phase-2 deployment path. On-chain, VaultRolePolicyManager treats policy id 0 as a permissive no-op, so a creator can enter 0 to bypass an otherwise configured nonzero role policy, such as owner EOA or allowlist requirements. This weakens deployment guardrails for vault creation and can allow deployment configurations the operator explicitly intended to block.

title: Stale registry owner authorizes Ajna automation control
description: The updated control endpoint now fetches the Ajna registry row and authorizes the caller against `registryRow.ownerAddress`. That owner value is populated from deployment/session data and stored in `public.ajna_vaults`; it is not refreshed from the current onchain owner during control requests. If a creator coin or vault ownership is transferred, the previous owner can still authenticate as their own address and pass this new check, while the new owner can be denied. The stale owner can then change automation status and movement caps, e.g. pausing/halt automation or enabling live keeper moves contrary to the current owner's intent. The prior code used `resolveCoinPartiesAndOwner(creatorToken)` at request time, which read the current onchain owner, so this stale-snapshot authorization issue is introduced by this commit.

title: CRE dependency audit removed from security CI
description: The security-scanning workflow now audits the root, frontend, and docs-site lockfiles, but no longer runs `pnpm --dir cre audit --audit-level high`. The CRE automation stack is a separate Node package with its own `cre/pnpm-lock.yaml` and runtime dependencies used by keeper/automation workflows. Because the root install/audit does not cover this separate lockfile, future high or critical vulnerable dependencies in the CRE keeper code can pass the blocking security CI. This is not an immediate runtime exploit in this diff, and the repository-wide gitleaks jobs still provide secret scanning, but the commit does introduce a security control regression for code that can operate with keeper credentials and onchain-write authority.

title: Unbounded avatar render cache enables memory DoS
description: The commit introduces an unauthenticated image-rendering route that accepts attacker-controlled `size` and `signatureText` query parameters and passes them to `renderHermitAvatarBuffer`. That helper normalizes the signature only to 24 characters, then uses `${size}:${signatureText}` as a cache key in a module-level `Map<string, Buffer>`. There is no TTL, LRU eviction, maximum entry count, or aggregate byte limit. Because `signatureText` has a very large input space, an attacker can continuously request unique values, especially at size 1024, causing the service to repeatedly run the expensive Sharp/SVG renderer and permanently retain each PNG Buffer for the lifetime of the warm serverless instance. The per-IP rate limit slows the attack but does not bound memory growth across windows or distributed clients. This can crash or degrade the catch-all API function via resource exhaustion.

title: AlfaClub /gmeow bypasses X posting authorization
description: The commit adds automatic X posting for Hermit /gmeow results. The AlfaClub bridge intentionally routes slash-command /gmeow messages from room senders into executeCommand with an alfaclub:<roomId> chatId, and executeCommand intentionally allows Hermit commands for any AlfaClub room user. The new /gmeow posting branch then calls postTweetFromSystem directly. That helper calls the low-level postTweet function, bypassing handleTwitterCommand's existing authorization controls, where /x post requires ADMIN/OWNER and --confirm. If the feature flag and Twitter credentials are configured, a low-privileged room participant can trigger official-account tweets, with content influenced by the /gmeow prompt/Pinata draft, subject only to the per-group one-minute rate limit.

title: Launch script exposes production secrets to build tools
description: scripts/launch.sh first validates that sensitive production variables such as AUTH_SESSION_SECRET, DATABASE_URL, DEPLOY_SESSION_TOKEN_HMAC_SECRET, PRIVY_APP_SECRET, PRIVY_WALLET_AUTHORIZATION_KEY, and optional DEPLOY_SOLANA_REGISTRATION_SECRET are present in the current shell. It then runs package-manager and build/test tooling with the inherited environment. Unlike the Vitest invocation, which explicitly uses env -i, the pnpm install/lint/typecheck/build and forge commands receive all of these secrets. Dependency lifecycle scripts, compromised build plugins, or any local build tooling executed by those commands can read and exfiltrate the production secrets. This is especially risky for pnpm install because npm package lifecycle hooks are a known supply-chain execution point.

title: Solana fallback reconciles only once per day
description: The new `/api/keeper/jobs/enqueue-solana-reconcile` cron endpoint defaults `KEEPER_SOLANA_RECONCILE_CHECKPOINT_PREFIX` to `YYYY-MM-DD`. It then builds checkpoint keys as `<date>:<action>` and sends them to `/api/cre/keeper/solana/reconcile`. That existing reconcile handler treats any previously completed `(workflow, checkpointKey)` as already processed and returns without calling the Solana orchestrator. As a result, once the first run of a day completes for actions such as `relay_entries`, `settle_fees`, or `winner_relay`, every later 15-minute cron run for that action uses the same checkpoint and is skipped until the next UTC day. In a CRE outage, the fallback intended to keep Solana lottery entries, fee settlement, winner relay, and other keeper duties moving can silently stop processing fresh activity for up to 24 hours. This can delay or misattribute lottery/fee-related protocol operations, though it does not directly let an attacker drain vault assets.

title: Public Supabase views bypass RLS-protected indexer tables
description: The new migration correctly enables and forces RLS on zora_csw_indexer_state and the underlying zora_csw_owners / zora_csw_owner_class tables are documented and configured as service-role-only. However, it then creates normal public views over those tables. In Supabase/Postgres, views are security-definer by default unless created with security_invoker=true, and Supabase public-schema objects are commonly exposed to anon/authenticated API roles. As a result, anon/authenticated callers may be able to query these views through the Supabase REST API and bypass the intended RLS boundary, learning indexer checkpoint/freshness, backlog, wallet-class breakdown, and enrichment throughput data. The views should either be created with security_invoker=true so underlying RLS applies, or SELECT should be explicitly revoked from anon/authenticated and granted only to service_role/admin roles.

title: Runbook may leak decrypted Vercel production secrets
description: The updated Vercel production env plan instructs operators to run `vercel env pull /tmp/.env.vercel-prod-pre-mutation --environment production` specifically for "broadcast-evidence capture" and then says to remove the "local decrypted env file after evidence capture". Vercel env pulls contain decrypted production environment variables, and this same file identifies `AMOE_LEDGER_PUBLISHER_PRIVATE_KEY` as a production secret. The wider deployment instructions require appending broadcast evidence to a docs file and committing it in a follow-up PR. This creates a realistic operator-induced secret disclosure path: decrypted production env contents may be copied into the evidence document or attached to the evidence PR. The previous wording explicitly limited the pull to local verification "without committing or sharing secrets"; this commit removes that safety framing and replaces it with evidence-capture language.

title: Orphan address guard misses no-0x runtime defaults
description: This commit adds a CI guard intended to prevent stale v1.10.1 orphan addresses from remaining in the repo, but the guard builds its grep pattern only from 0x-prefixed address strings. The codebase's shared contract defaults deliberately use addr('hexWithout0x'), so the existing Base lotteryManager default still points to the orphaned 0xd593... address while not matching the new guard. The server API falls back to BASE_DEFAULTS.lotteryManager when LOTTERY_MANAGER is unset, so a production or staging environment missing the override can continue binding AMOE/lottery requests to the orphan manager. This undermines the cleanup sweep and allows current or future runtime orphan references to bypass CI simply by omitting the 0x prefix or constructing the string.

title: Manual health workflow can leak the cron secret
description: The new GitHub Actions workflow has a manual workflow_dispatch trigger and then uses actions/checkout without pinning the checkout to a trusted ref. For workflow_dispatch runs, GitHub allows the dispatcher to select a branch/ref, and actions/checkout defaults to that ref. The job then injects the repository secret ALFACLUB_HEALTH_CRON_SECRET and executes frontend/scripts/alfaclub-auth-health-monitor.mjs from the checked-out repository. A user with permission to push a branch and manually run workflows could create a branch that modifies that script to print or POST the secret, dispatch this workflow on that branch, and obtain the cron secret without passing code review or merging to the protected default branch. That cron secret is used for cron-secret-gated AlfaClub endpoints and other operational automation, so leakage expands access beyond the intended monitor.

title: Gitleaks allowlist hides generic secrets in *.example.env
description: The new allowlist entries suppress the generic-api-key rule for cre/secrets.example.env and, more broadly, for any future file matching [A-Za-z0-9_-]+.example.env. Although provider-specific detectors still run, many operational credentials in this repo are custom or generic secrets, such as KEEPR_API_KEY, DefiLlama API keys, Privy app secrets, and raw EVM keeper private keys. Those may only be caught by the generic detector. As a result, a real non-provider-specific credential accidentally or intentionally committed to cre/secrets.example.env or another *.example.env file can bypass the configured full-history and PR Gitleaks gates.

title: Refund cron can refund burns that may still settle
description: The refund scanner only excludes `amoe_zk_submissions` rows whose state is exactly `settled`. That means old burns with related submissions in active or retryable states such as `proven`, `broadcast`, or `manager_declined` are still selected for refund. The subsequent refund insert is unconditional and does not atomically re-check submission state before restoring credits. Because the migration makes `amoe_entry_refund` count toward `points_amoe_eligible_balance`, the user can regain off-chain AMOE eligibility while the original submission can still later settle on chain. This breaks the accounting invariant that each on-chain AMOE entry consumes credits exactly once. The issue is especially relevant because the ledger publisher can build burn ledger leaves from submissions with `twitter_credit_nullifier_hex IS NOT NULL` without requiring `state='settled'`, so a non-settled retryable submission may already have a usable burn leaf. A safer implementation should only refund burns that have no active/retryable submission, or that are in a terminal non-settled state and cannot be reused, and should perform the refund insert with the state/refund checks in the same SQL statement or transaction.

title: Chat score hydration leaks XMTP peer addresses
description: The commit adds Ethos score badges to recent chat conversations and chat windows. For each rendered peer address, the new `useEthosScore` hook calls `/api/v1/chat/search?q=<address>`. That endpoint invokes `getCachedEthosScoreByAddress`, which calls the external Ethos API and inserts the address into `chat_directory_profiles`. This means simply opening the chat bar/rail/window can disclose a user's XMTP conversation peer addresses to the 4626 backend, server logs, database, and Ethos, even when those peers did not opt into availability and even when the score is only decorative. The leak is especially visible in `ChatBar`, which renders all conversations and hydrates a badge for each DM peer.

title: Unauthenticated Hermit health leaks runtime state
description: The commit adds a new long-lived Hermit HTTP health server. Its health responses include the full in-memory runtime state, including the configured AlfaClub room id, bridge start reason, timestamps, recent tick counters, recent message processing errors, and the last bridge error. There is no health-detail token, caller authentication, or redaction before returning this data. If the Railway service is reachable publicly or through a shared/internal network, an unauthenticated caller can monitor private AlfaClub room activity and operational failures. The existing Eliza health endpoint has a detailed-health access gate, but this new Hermit endpoint always returns detailed state.

title: AMOE retries can relay entries without burning credits
description: The initial ZK submit path only debits AMOE credits after a successful relay and markSettled call. If the relay reverts with ManagerDeclinedEntry, the handler stores the proof as retryable and returns 202 before any credit debit occurs. The new retry executor later rebuilds calldata and relays the stored proof, but on success it only calls markSettled and explicitly does not consume credits. This means a retry that finally succeeds can create an on-chain lottery entry without burning the user's credits. In addition, retrySubmissionById only permits rows in manager_declined, while markSettled only updates rows in broadcast or proven, so the post-relay markSettled call will throw after the transaction has already succeeded. That leaves the row stale and can cause repeated failed retries / relayer spend while still not charging the user.

title: DB error diagnostics can leak AlfaClub tokens to logs
description: The new describeDbError helper copies err.message and err.detail into the structured log payload with only length truncation. The affected catch blocks are reached after attempting to INSERT secret_value values that contain the AlfaClub chat JWT, Privy access token, or Privy refresh token. PostgreSQL errors are not guaranteed to keep these fields free of parameter data: for example, NOT NULL/check constraint failures can include `DETAIL: Failing row contains (...)`, and type/schema-drift errors can include the invalid input value. Because this commit was specifically added for schema/RLS/DB diagnostics, schema-drift failure modes are in scope and can cause the sensitive token material being persisted to appear in general observability logs. The public API response remains redacted, but the server-side log path can expose operational secrets to anyone with log access.

title: 403 room denial now fails open to live chat processing
description: The new isRoomHistoryAuthError() predicate treats room_history_failed:403 the same as 401. That predicate is then used both for retrying with an env JWT and, more importantly, for enabling the WebSocket live fallback. A 403 from the history API is an authorization decision: the token is authenticated but lacks permission for the configured room or has been revoked. After this change, if history returns 403 and wsLiveFallbackEnabled is true by default, the bridge marks liveFallbackActive, opens/keeps a WebSocket, drains queued live messages for the configured room, and passes them to executeCommandBatch(). executeCommandBatch() runs executeDeterministicCommand() before attempting to post a response, and the AlfaClub command family includes actions that can submit user operations such as buy-key or create-room. This creates a fail-open authorization path: revoking/removing the bot from a room at the history-API ACL layer no longer reliably stops the bridge from processing live messages if the WebSocket path is still delivering them or if a separate ingest JWT is configured. A safer change would retry a different known-good JWT on 403, but should not enter live fallback on a permission-denied/revoked-room response unless room authorization is independently revalidated.

title: Weak v3 swap token check bypasses paymaster swap policy
description: In the new direct-v3 swap path, calls are accepted when the target is an allowed v3 router and selector is in the new allowed set. For those calls, token linkage is validated by `assertRawSwapPayloadReferencesToken`, which checks only whether the approved token hex appears anywhere in calldata. This is not semantic validation of `tokenIn`/`tokenOut`/path. Because ABI-encoded uint256 fields can be attacker-chosen, the approved token bytes can be injected into unrelated parameters (such as deadline or max-input fields), satisfying validation without actually constraining the traded token pair. This weakens paymaster policy guarantees and can be used to obtain sponsorship for swaps outside intended constraints, increasing paymaster abuse risk.

title: Trusted-setup script skips phase-1 ptau integrity verification
description: In `00-setup.sh`, the script only checks that `pot14_final.ptau` exists, then immediately uses it for `snarkjs groth16 setup`. There is no comparison against a manifest-pinned SHA-256. This is a security issue for a trusted setup: if an attacker can replace the ptau artifact (e.g., compromised download source, poisoned local artifact, or supply-chain tampering), the ceremony can proceed with an untrusted phase-1 transcript. The runbook explicitly claims the script verifies ptau hash, but the implementation does not. Given these artifacts are used to generate the production verifier key/contract, accepting a malicious ptau can undermine proof soundness assumptions and potentially enable forged proofs.

title: Hermit meme list exposes room data to any authenticated user
description: The commit introduces `GET /api/v1/chat/hermit/memes/list`. The handler requires a valid session address, but room authorization is evaluated against `getHermitOwnerAddress()` (configured owner) rather than the caller. As a result, any authenticated user can query memes for any room that is allowed for the Hermit owner (via explicit room allowlist or owner holdings), even if the caller is unrelated to that room. This creates an authorization gap and enables cross-room data disclosure (room meme URLs/CIDs/captions/tags), and room-id enumeration through response differences.

title: AMOE relayer can mint arbitrary lottery entries without proof
description: This commit introduces `processAmoeEntry`, which accepts `buyer`, `creatorCoin`, and `pointsBurnedAsUSD` from an allowlisted relayer and immediately routes them into lottery entry creation. The only authorization check is `msg.sender == authorizedAmoeRelayer`; there is no on-chain verification that points were actually burned, no nonce/replay protection, and no cryptographic binding between off-chain AMOE claims and on-chain entry creation. A compromised or malicious relayer key can submit arbitrary high-value AMOE entries for attacker-controlled buyers and materially increase win frequency (up to configured caps), enabling jackpot extraction and potential sponsorship budget drain.

title: Paywall bypass via Stripe checkout pending activation
description: The Stripe checkout flow inserts a `creator_strategy_features` row with `status='pending'` before payment is verified. The paywall resolver treats any `pending` or `active` row as paid and is now used by the paymaster to approve Phase‑3 strategy weights. An attacker can start a Stripe checkout (no payment), obtain a pending row, and then submit a deployment UserOp with non‑zero weights; the paymaster accepts it because the plan sees the pending activation. This bypasses the paid‑feature gate and enables free strategy deployments until payment verification/provisioning catches up.

title: Keepr execute skips trust-zone auth when env secret missing
description: In the keepr action execution handler, the trust-zone header verification is now conditional on the zone secret being non-empty. If the trust-zone secret environment variable is missing or empty, the code skips requireOptionalHeaderEnvAuth entirely and proceeds to execute actions. The helper itself is designed to fail closed when an env var is absent, but the new guard bypasses that behavior. This reintroduces a fail-open path on misconfigured deployments, letting any caller with the KEEPR_API_KEY execute actions across trust zones without the intended per-zone key separation.

title: Trend reserve UserOps bypass spend caps for zero-value calls
description: The commit introduces reserveTrendTickerViaUserOp, which constructs a TrendCoin deploy call with value 0 and forwards valueWei: 0 to submitUserOpOrRefuse. The submitUserOpOrRefuse cap logic only evaluates caps and records daily spend based on valueWei, and it skips recording when valueWei is 0. This means trend reserve deployments are not capped at all, despite the comments implying caps/daily ledger enforcement. A malicious or compromised ADMIN/OWNER can repeatedly reserve new tickers to consume paymaster gas without hitting limits, draining paymaster funds or causing availability issues.

title: Waitlist bootstrap leaks canonical email on wallet collision
description: The commit adds wallet-collision checks that read a canonical profile email from the database and build an IdentityRecoveryRequiredError containing that email. The waitlist bootstrap handler now returns this canonicalEmail directly in its JSON response for WALLET_BOUND_TO_CANONICAL_EMAIL_PROFILE. This exposes PII (verified email address) to any actor who can authenticate with the wallet, and could leak email associations for compromised or shared wallets. A safer approach would be to return a generic recovery-required message without the canonical email or only reveal it after stronger verification.

title: AMOE waitlist points inflate spendable lottery credits
description: The commit adds `amoe_entry` and `amoe_checkin` awards that insert positive amounts into the shared `points` table for canonical profiles. The AMOE credit calculator in `lotteryAmoe.ts` uses a catch‑all `ELSE amount * 0.30` branch, so any new sources not explicitly excluded (including these new AMOE waitlist sources) are treated as credits. As a result, submitting lottery entries or daily check-ins now also increases the spendable credit pool, creating a feedback loop that lets a user gain more entries than intended and undermines the separation between waitlist points and AMOE credits.

title: Paymaster allowlist bypass for deploy-session selfcalls
description: The paymaster validation no longer enforces the creator allowlist when the call mode is `deploy_session_setup`. That mode is triggered for self-calls on the smart wallet that add or remove owners. Because allowlisting is the primary guard against unauthorized paymaster sponsorship, this change allows any authenticated session owner (even if not allowlisted) to obtain sponsored gas for owner-management calls. An attacker can create multiple wallets/sessions and repeatedly invoke these operations to drain paymaster budget or consume sponsorship limits, weakening the intended access control.

title: Auth handoff URL auto-redeem enables login CSRF
description: The updated useSiweAuth hook reads a cv_handoff query parameter, redeems it via /api/auth/handoff/redeem, and immediately writes the returned session token (and optionally Privy token) into browser storage/session state. Because handoff codes are bearer tokens that can be created by any authenticated user and redeemed by whoever possesses them, an attacker can generate a handoff code for their own account and send a link like https://app.4626.fun/?cv_handoff=<code> to a victim. When the victim opens the link, their browser is silently logged into the attacker’s account (session fixation/login CSRF). This can lead to unintended actions or wallet linking occurring under the attacker’s account.

title: External swap path lets keeper drain router token balances
description: `convertViaExternalAndQueue` delegates to an allowlisted `swapTarget` with arbitrary calldata and only checks that the router’s creatorCoin balance increased by at least `minCreatorOut`. Because `minCreatorOut` is provided by the caller (keeper) and can be set to a tiny value, a malicious or compromised keeper (or an automated keeper tricked by a malicious quote service) can craft calldata for a permissive swap target (e.g., a universal router) to transfer `tokenIn` to an attacker-controlled address and send back only dust creatorCoin. This bypasses the earlier fixed-path constraint and enables theft of the router’s payout balances once external swap approvals are enabled.

title: Operator can sweep LP reserve before auction launch
description: The commit adds residual sweep functions gated by `_requireOperatorSweep`, which only checks `block.number >= lastSweepBlock`. `lastSweepBlock` is initialized to 0 and only set during `_launchAuctionInternal`. However, DeploymentBatcher now transfers the 20% LP reserve to the strategy before any auction is launched. Because `lastSweepBlock` is still 0, the operator (set to protocolTreasury) can immediately call `sweepResidualAuctionToken`/`sweepResidualCurrency` and drain the reserve, breaking later `launchAuctionWithReserve`/`migrate()` or siphoning funds earlier than intended. This bypasses the intended sweep delay and enables privileged early withdrawal of reserved assets.

title: SSRF bypass via IPv4-mapped IPv6 in ERC8004 review
description: The paid review service (`buildErc8004TechnicalReview`) accepts `registrationUrl`/`endpoint` from the request and fetches them after checking for forbidden hosts. The IPv6 filter only treats `::ffff:` prefixes as private when the remainder is dotted IPv4. IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses written in hex (e.g., `http://[::ffff:7f00:1]/` for 127.0.0.1 or `http://[::ffff:a9fe:a9fe]/` for 169.254.169.254) are not recognized as private, so `isHostnameResolutionSafe` returns true and the fetch proceeds. This bypass enables authenticated callers to SSRF internal/metadata endpoints and potentially exfiltrate JSON responses via the review payload.

title: Private DM flag bypasses Telegram chat allowlist
description: The commit adds TELEGRAM_ALLOW_PRIVATE_DMS/TELEGRAM_ALLOW_ALL_PRIVATE_DMS and treats any private chat as allowed when the flag is true. This bypasses the existing allowlist and admin-DM restriction, so any Telegram account can DM the bot and reach the command execution path. Because the handler resolves command context using TELEGRAM_DEFAULT_GROUP_ID and TELEGRAM_DEFAULT_SENDER_WALLET fallbacks, an untrusted DM can be routed into a real vault context and inherit a privileged sender wallet if defaults are set. That enables unauthorized execution of sensitive commands (e.g., /send, /keepr lock/unlock, /coin actions) through the bot once private DMs are enabled.

title: Charm strategy withdrawal can be DoSed by swap failure
description: The updated Charm strategy makes every withdrawal (and emergency withdrawal) perform a mandatory USDC→CREATOR swap via `_swapUsdcToCreatorRequired`. That helper reverts if the TWAP is unavailable or if the router swap fails. Because Charm withdrawals typically return a USDC leg, any actor who can push spot price beyond the TWAP-based `minOut` (or otherwise cause swaps/observations to fail) can force the strategy to revert, preventing vault withdrawals entirely. This is a new availability risk introduced by the change to required swaps and removal of the previous fail-open behavior.

title: XMTP agent exposes OpenClaw intel tools without auth
description: The commit wires the XMTP message router to iterate over all plugin actions and adds wallet intelligence/reputation/lens actions that directly call the OpenClaw execute endpoint. These handlers perform no sender allowlisting or rate limiting and default to storing results. The OpenClaw tooling uses paid/privileged API keys (e.g., DeBank/Etherscan) and storage uploads. As a result, any XMTP participant can repeatedly invoke /intel, /funder, /portfolio, or /labels to exhaust API quotas or drive storage costs, degrading availability and incurring unexpected spend.

title: Persisted canonical wallet mapping blocks revocation
description: The new wallet sync logic reads the profile’s stored primary/canonical/embedded addresses and re-injects them into the current Privy-linked wallet classification. This means a wallet that a user has unlinked (or attempted to revoke) is still treated as the canonical or primary wallet and is re-flagged in profile_wallets on each sync. Ownership checks for deploy-session creation rely on the is_canonical_smart_wallet flag and membership in profile_wallets, so a previously linked wallet can continue to satisfy those checks even after revocation, enabling continued access to creator deployment flows or other privileged actions tied to canonical-wallet status.

title: Charm factory deployment leaves vault governance external
description: The previous deployment flow created the Charm vault locally and immediately called initializeAndTransfer to assign governance/keeper to the protocol. The refactor now relies on Charm’s external factory (createVault) and does not perform any governance transfer afterward. The factory interface only accepts a manager parameter; governance remains with the factory or its governance address. If Charm’s governance/factory is compromised or upgraded maliciously, it can change vault parameters/strategy or siphon protocol fees, creating a new trust dependency and enabling hostile control over vault behavior.

title: Unauthenticated waitlist upsert enables data tampering
description: The newly added waitlist API accepts unauthenticated POSTs and performs an UPSERT keyed only on the email address. Because there is no authentication or ownership proof, any caller who knows a target email can update stored fields such as primary_wallet, persona, and Farcaster metadata. The response also exposes a `created` boolean derived from xmax, which reveals whether the email already exists in the database, enabling email enumeration. This is a data integrity and privacy issue for waitlist/PII data; the endpoint should be insert-only or require verification tokens for updates and avoid disclosing existence.

title: Room ID ignored after pools redirect
description: The commit changes legacy pools/liquidity aliases from the room liquidity tab to the new /explore/pools page while preserving the original query string. However, AlfaClubLiquidityPools only reads the pool query parameter. It does not read roomId, does not filter pools by that room, and does not pass roomId as initialTokenId into AlfaClubLpWriteConsole. As a result, links such as /pools?roomId=9 can land on the global pools page with the first available pool selected, or with a create console that is no longer room-seeded. This is a functional regression and could cause user confusion when following room-specific liquidity links, but it does not appear to bypass authentication or directly authorize unwanted transactions.

title: Public cache can leak denied viewer wallet addresses
description: The commit adds room-access checking to /api/v1/alfaclub/room-timeline and includes the resulting chatAccess object in every successful response. When a signed-in viewer does not have room access, includeChat is false, so the endpoint sets Cache-Control to public, s-maxage=45. However, the denied chatAccess object can contain the viewer's walletAddress. Because the response is public and is not varied on Cookie/Authorization, a shared CDN/cache may store a denied authenticated user's response and serve the same URL to other users, disclosing that wallet address and access status. The endpoint should either omit walletAddress/user-specific chatAccess fields from public responses or mark any response computed from an authenticated session as private/no-store.

title: Room avatars bypass external image proxy safeguards
description: AlfaClub room image URLs are read from external room metadata and returned to the frontend without URL or content validation. Before this change, RoomDiscoveryTray attempted to route those URLs through the external image proxy. The new code trims room.imageUrl and assigns it directly to an . This bypasses the existing proxy's protections: URL scheme/host validation, private-address checks, redirect checks, MIME allowlisting, magic-byte sniffing, SVG rejection, a 2 MB size cap, and forced nosniff headers. An attacker who can influence AlfaClub room metadata can make visitors' browsers directly request attacker-controlled or otherwise unsafe allowed image URLs, enabling visitor IP/referrer tracking and potentially client-side resource exhaustion or unsafe image handling that the proxy was designed to prevent. React attribute escaping limits this to image loading behavior rather than straightforward DOM XSS, so the impact is low.

title: Room avatars bypass external image proxy
description: SelectedRoomAvatar now assigns room.imageUrl directly to an . The image URL originates from AlfaClub room metadata and is passed through the trading-rooms API without URL, MIME, or size validation. The repository already has a hardened /api/image/external proxy that validates URL schemes/hosts, rejects unsafe targets, enforces a raster-image MIME allowlist, caps image size, sniffs bytes, and sets nosniff. Rendering raw third-party URLs bypasses those controls and can cause clients visiting /rooms to fetch attacker-influenced image URLs directly, leaking client network metadata such as IP/user-agent/origin referrer to allowed image hosts and losing the proxy's content/size restrictions. CSP img-src limits the destination set, so this is low severity and does not affect onchain funds or authentication.

title: XMTP test path can revoke the protocol agent inbox
description: The commit exposes `/hermit alert xmtp test`, which immediately calls `sendProtocolAgentXmtpDm` for the caller. That helper constructs a new `XmtpService` and calls `xmtp.start()` for every one-shot DM. `XmtpService.start()` contains a post-create guard that calls `revokeAllOtherInstallations()` when the inbox has 8 or more installations, regardless of the caller passing `revokeOtherInstallations: false`. Because the one-shot sender uses a separate local DB path and may run in serverless or otherwise non-persistent environments, repeated invocations can create additional protocol-agent installations until the guard revokes all other installations, including the long-running protocol/Eliza XMTP agent. The current one-shot instance is then stopped, leaving the primary agent unable to receive messages until it re-registers. This is mainly an availability/abuse issue for the XMTP agent lane, not a funds-at-risk issue.

title: Internal wallet and Railway identifiers committed
description: A new internal operations document commits production operational identifiers, including the Railway project UUID and the Privy server wallet ID used for the protocol/canonical CSW. These values are not private keys or standalone authentication secrets, but they are sensitive operational metadata. If the repository or internal docs are exposed beyond trusted operators, an attacker gains precise targets for Privy/Railway API abuse attempts, credential-stuffing, phishing, or chaining with any separately leaked app secret / wallet authorization key.

title: Unbounded in-memory reply-claim cache enables DoS
description: The new command dedupe path records every claimed `(roomId,messageId)` in `inMemoryClaimedReplyKeys`. This Set is module-global and has no TTL, maximum size, or cleanup outside of a test-only reset helper. Every command processed by `executeCommandBatch` and every inverse-chat intent processed by `executeInverseAkitaChatReactionBatch` calls `tryClaimCommandReply`, which adds a unique key on successful DB claim and also when the DB is unavailable or errors. A user able to post many unique command messages in configured AlfaClub command rooms can cause the long-running bridge process to retain an ever-growing number of strings until memory pressure or process restart. The database ledger already persists dedupe state, so the additional unbounded in-memory cache creates an avoidable memory exhaustion risk.

title: Auth health flags new Privy refresh writers as anomalous
description: Token refreshes are now recorded with new writer values such as `vercel-cron-privy-refresher` and `hermit-privy-refresher`. However, `evaluateWriterAnomaly` still only accepts the old `privy-token-refresher` and other legacy/admin writer names. As a result, normal successful token rotation by either the Vercel backup cron or the Hermit primary refresher will be classified as `unknown_writer`. The external auth-health monitor treats any live JWT writer anomaly as a hard failure, so healthy deployments will page/fail monitoring after this change. This does not directly expose token material or bypass authentication, but it degrades the reliability of the auth-health security monitor and can create alert fatigue or mask real writer anomalies.

title: Public docs publish internal audit findings
description: The new audit files are placed under docs/audits/ rather than docs/_internal/. The docs-site sync script includes all markdown under docs/ by default and excludes docs/_internal/** plus only selected audit subtrees; it does not exclude the newly added deep-risk-audit-2026-06*.md files. The committed report explicitly states it was sourced from docs/_internal/audits-workpapers and then rewritten into a public report set, and it includes detailed exploitable information such as unthrottled mutating endpoints, paymaster sponsorship limiter weaknesses, unauthenticated relay proxy behavior, exact API routes, and open launch blockers. If the production docs build runs, these files can be copied to the public docs site and indexed/searchable despite representing unrepaired security workpapers.

title: Docs build reintroduces vulnerable js-yaml parser
description: The docs-site previously forced js-yaml to 4.2.0 through its local pnpm overrides. This commit removes that override while the docs build pipeline still uses gray-matter to parse Markdown frontmatter from synced documentation sources. The resulting lockfile now resolves gray-matter to js-yaml 3.14.2. If an attacker can influence Markdown/frontmatter processed by the docs build or CI pipeline, this reintroduces the vulnerable YAML parser version that the override was pinning away, potentially impacting the build environment and any deployment secrets available there. Restore the js-yaml override or upgrade the frontmatter tooling so it uses the patched parser version.

title: OVault delegate guard misses whitespace delegate calls
description: The commit introduces `scripts/check-ovault-delegate-epilogues.mjs` to prevent CreatorOVault nonReentrant functions from calling `_delegate()`. However, the actual detector searches each line with `line.indexOf('_delegate(', pos)`, which only matches the exact token sequence `_delegate(`. Solidity permits whitespace and comments between an identifier and the call parenthesis, e.g. `_delegate (_coreModule);` or `_delegate\n(_coreModule);`. Those forms still call the same unsafe `_delegate` helper, but the guard does not report them. I verified this by temporarily replacing one `_delegateAndReturn(_coreModule);` in a nonReentrant CreatorOVault function with `_delegate (_coreModule);`; the script still printed that all 33 nonReentrant functions passed. This does not introduce an immediate deployed-contract vulnerability in the current source, but it weakens a security CI control intended to prevent a known P1 permanent-DoS class from being reintroduced.

title: AMOE ZK assets moved to shadowed Vercel function
description: The AMOE ZK submit handler resolves prover artifacts from bundled files under server/_lib/lottery/amoe-zk-assets when AMOE_ZK_WASM_PATH and AMOE_ZK_ZKEY_PATH are not set. Before this commit those files were included in the api/[...path].ts bundle. The commit removes that include and adds a new api/v1/lottery/amoe/submit-zk.ts function with the assets included there. However, frontend/vercel.json still has a generic /api/(.*) route before the filesystem handler, so requests to /api/v1/lottery/amoe/submit-zk are rewritten to /api/[...path] instead of the new standalone function. As a result, production requests still execute the catch-all handler, but that bundle no longer contains the wasm/zkey files needed to generate PLONK proofs. In environments relying on the bundled fallback paths, valid AMOE ZK submissions will fail during proof generation, causing an availability failure for lottery entry submission.

title: Public page exposes counter-trade internals
description: A new `/arena/counter-trade-files` page is registered under the marketing/public route tree and renders hard-coded internal implementation details for the counter-trading bot. The page discloses exact server module names, runtime components, API handler filenames, database migration names, operator/admin UI locations, scripts, and runbook names. While it does not expose secrets or file contents by itself, it gives unauthenticated users a map of sensitive automation and trading infrastructure, including the cron/manual trigger handler and operational runbooks, which can materially aid endpoint enumeration and targeted attacks against the counter-trade lane.

title: Key-safety calculator misses zero-buy hostile holder raids
description: The calculator states it models the worst case where every key the user does not hold is hostile, but the raid model only evaluates an outside attacker who buys at least one fresh key. When the user is below veto control, existing hostile holders may already satisfy the 50% vote threshold and can dissolve/distribute the room with zero incremental key purchase. Because `analyzeRaid` forces `minAttackKeys` to at least 1 and `raidProfit` only counts payout on newly bought keys, modest pots/donations can be marked as `raidUnprofitable`, causing `evaluateKeyDefense` to return `economically-protected` despite the existing hostile majority being able to take the pot. For example, with 30 total keys and the user holding 10, the other 20 keys already clear a 50% vote threshold; a small donation may make a one-key outside raid unprofitable while still being extractable by current hostile holders.

title: Global alert cooldown can suppress other users' risk alerts
description: The commit introduces alert mode for user-silo defense when no Hyperliquid API-wallet key is configured. The anti-spam state is a module-global Map, but the cooldown key is built as `[silo, coin, action.type]` and does not include the room, opted-in sender, or protected wallet/master address. In any alert-mode deployment with multiple active opted-in users, the first risky BTC `defend_reduce` alert, for example, sets `user|BTC|defend_reduce`; subsequent risky BTC defend alerts for other users during the 30-minute window are skipped entirely, including both room posting and skipped-row ledgering. A malicious or competing opted-in user could intentionally trigger an alert first to suppress another user's advisory alert, reducing the availability of this liquidation-risk warning. The intended room 1659 single-actor setup limits practical impact there, but the code path is generic and runs for all active opt-ins when user-silo defense is enabled without a key.

title: Malformed fill time can abort LLM-gated trades
description: When the optional counter-trade LLM advisor is enabled, runCounterTradeLoop registers a new fill event in the ledger and then calls applyCounterTradeLlmGate before placing the trade. applyCounterTradeLlmGate constructs the prompt before entering its try/catch, and buildCounterTradeAdvisorPrompt calls new Date(context.fill.time).toISOString(). getUserFillsByTimeDetailed only checks that the upstream timestamp is finite, not that it is within JavaScript Date's valid range. A finite but out-of-range timestamp therefore throws a RangeError before the advisor can apply its configured failure policy. The exception bubbles to the per-identity catch, aborting the rest of that identity scan; because the event was already registered, that candidate will not be retried. This is a limited availability/integrity issue for the optional LLM-gated counter-trade loop if malformed fill data can enter through the external Hyperliquid feed or configured proxy.

title: CI security gates downgraded to non-blocking telemetry
description: This change does not modify runtime protocol code, but it does introduce a security control regression in the repository's merge/push workflow. Full-history gitleaks previously ran on every PR, push, and schedule; it is now limited to schedule/manual runs and marked continue-on-error, so it no longer blocks any merge path. The default Slither job previously parsed Slither JSON and failed the job on high-impact findings for all normal PR/push executions. That failure step has been removed, leaving Slither report-only except for the separate launch/* gate. As a result, high-impact smart-contract findings introduced through ordinary branches targeting main/master can pass CI unless caught manually.

title: Blank HERMIT env can override legacy relay disable
description: The commit intends HERMIT_* variables to replace ALFACLUB_* while keeping legacy aliases supported. However, several lookups use `??` before trimming/parsing. Because environment variables are strings, a configured-but-empty `HERMIT_TELEGRAM_*` value is not nullish and prevents fallback to the non-empty legacy variable. For the webhook secret/token this causes a migration-time outage. More concerningly, `HERMIT_TELEGRAM_RELAY_ENABLED=''` shadows `ALFACLUB_TELEGRAM_RELAY_ENABLED='0'`; `parseBoolWithDefault` then treats the empty value as unset and uses the auto-enable fallback. If a bot token and chat destination are present via either HERMIT or legacy variables, `telegramRelayEnabled` becomes true and ingested AlfaClub messages are sent to Telegram despite the legacy opt-out.

title: Orphan-address sweep now passes while scanning only amoe
description: The orphan-address guard is intended to prevent stale/deprecated deployment addresses from being referenced outside an explicit whitelist. However, because the script lives at amoe/tools/ci/check_no_orphan_addresses.sh, its ROOT_DIR calculation using ../.. resolves to <repo>/amoe, not the repository root. The script then cd's into that subtree and runs git grep from there, so it only searches files under amoe/. Before this commit, the guard failed on its own script references because git grep emitted paths such as tools/ci/check_no_orphan_addresses.sh. The newly added whitelist entries make those amoe-relative hits acceptable, causing the workflow to report success while still missing references elsewhere in the repository. A malicious or mistaken change could add one of the orphaned lottery/AMOE addresses in root-level deployment, keeper, frontend, or docs paths and this CI guard would not detect it.

title: Most-active chat sender is mislabeled as room host
description: The new pickEffectiveHostAddress helper falls back to the most active sender whenever the resolved host address is absent from the current message window. For room 1659, the resolved address is the Hyperliquid portfolio wallet, not necessarily the actual chat sender, so this fallback is likely to run in normal use. An attacker who can post many room messages can become the computed effectiveHost, causing the API to return isHost=true for their messages. The frontend then treats those messages as host-chat, includes them in the Host only filter, and displays host badges on chart overlays/tooltips. This is not a direct asset-drain issue, but it compromises the integrity of a trading/social-signal surface and can be used to impersonate the host in the UI.

title: Alert test leaks linked Telegram chat ID
description: The commit adds a Telegram alert test path that resolves the caller wallet's linked Telegram identifier and sends a DM. On success, it returns `Telegram alert test sent ✅ (chat ${chatId}).`. For AlfaClub room invocations, that returned text is sent back to the room as the bot reply. This exposes a user's linked Telegram user/chat ID to other room participants, creating an avoidable privacy/account-correlation leak. Existing status handling only reports whether Telegram is linked and does not disclose the identifier; the new success reply should omit or mask the chat ID.

title: Hermit X posts can fall back to shared Twitter creds
description: This commit changes postTweetFromSystem to force strict Hermit-only OAuth1 credentials when Hermit-specific Twitter credentials are configured. However, hasAnyHermitTwitterOauth1EnvConfigured returns true only when all four HERMIT_TWITTER_* variables are present, despite its name and fail-closed purpose. If an operator configures any subset of HERMIT_TWITTER_* variables, strictHermitOnly remains false and readTwitterOauth1Credentials can fall back to X_* or TWITTER_* credentials. In deployments where Hermit media auto-cross-posting is enabled, a user who can run Hermit media commands can cause posts to be made with the shared/operator Twitter credentials rather than the intended Hermit account, or can trigger mixed-credential failures. The helper should return true if any Hermit OAuth1 variable is present so partial Hermit configuration fails closed with missing HERMIT_* keys.

title: Route token logos can spoof core assets by symbol
description: The new route logo fallback resolves official Uniswap logos solely from the token symbol. In buildSwapRouteTokenLookup, a route leg with an explicit non-core address but symbol USDC, WETH, ETH, or ZORA will keep the non-core resolvedAddress while receiving the official core token logo. SwapRoutePopover then passes that logo as the preferred image and marks the avatar as core based only on the symbol. Since route data comes from external quote providers and token metadata can be attacker-influenced, a malicious or compromised quote/metadata source could make a counterfeit or unrelated route hop appear visually as a trusted core asset in the route popover. This appears limited to UI deception in route details and does not directly alter swap calldata or authorization.

title: Sampling makes Telegram action tokens unusable
description: The new guard in `createTelegramActionToken` returns a random token before inserting its hash and intent payload into `telegram_action_tokens` whenever `shouldSampleEvent('telegram_action_tokens', ...)` is false. However, `consumeTelegramActionToken` only accepts tokens by updating/selecting this database row. There is no stateless fallback or signed payload validation. Therefore skipped rows are not merely lost telemetry; they are the authorization state for Telegram trade/deploy/status callbacks. Because sampling is deterministic on `${userId}:${actionType}`, affected users/actions can be permanently unable to confirm that action while `TELEMETRY_SAMPLE_RATE` or the per-table override is less than 1.

title: Hermit container now runs as root
description: The only code change replaces the previous startup command that used `gosu node` with a root-executed shell-form CMD. Because the Dockerfile does not set `USER node`, Docker runs the command as the default root user. This is an introduced privilege-management regression: any future compromise of the Hermit agent, its TypeScript runtime, dependencies, or user-controlled chat/agent processing would execute with root privileges inside the container instead of the restricted `node` account. The service still installs `gosu` and the comments reference privilege dropping, but the final CMD no longer uses it.

title: Risk watcher now crashes from undeclared state variables
description: The new healthcheck state added lastError and consecutiveFailures, but the patch accidentally replaced the existing declarations for isShuttingDown, lastSuccessfulTick, and lastTickStatus instead of adding to them. Because this TypeScript file is executed as an ES module, reads or assignments to these undeclared identifiers throw ReferenceError at runtime. Continuous mode reaches while (!isShuttingDown) and exits before monitoring starts. The tick success and error paths also reference lastSuccessfulTick/lastTickStatus, so --once or imported tick execution can fail. If a healthcheck request reaches the handler, it reads lastSuccessfulTick/lastTickStatus as well. This disables the Railway risk watcher and its healthcheck/alerting behavior.

title: /bridge alias reaches write-capable AlfaClub subcommands
description: The commit adds a /bridge command head and maps it to the existing alfaclub family. The parser only special-cases an empty /bridge command to status; otherwise it strips /bridge and feeds the rest into the normal /alfa parser. Because that parser includes write-capable subcommands, inputs such as /bridge buy-key <tokenId> or /bridge create-room <payload> can reach the same UserOperation submission paths as /alfa buy-key and /alfa create-room. This contradicts the commit/docs/tests that describe /bridge as a bridge-health/status alias. Existing signer, TEE, and execution-context checks still apply, so this is not a direct unauthorized fund-drain, but it broadens a read-only operational alias into transaction-capable command surface and can defeat expectations or future policies that treat /bridge as safe/read-only.

title: Post-upgrade hook verification accepts partial bytecode
description: The changed post-upgrade verification predicate uses an OR match over `relay_entries|RelayEntries|SettleFees`. This means a dumped program containing `SettleFees` but lacking the required `relay_entries` instruction strings will still print `canonical relay_entries / settle_fees bytecode OK`. Because the script supports `--skip-build --execute`, this weakens the final deployed-bytecode check compared with the build-time check, which still requires `relay_entries`. A stale or wrong artifact could therefore be accepted after deployment, causing operators to configure keepers for canonical relay behavior even though the live hook may not support lottery entry relay. This is primarily an operational safety issue and requires control of the upgrade workflow/artifact, so impact is limited, but it can disrupt Solana lottery/fee relay behavior.

title: Static tray points cache can leak prior account data
description: The commit replaces the wallet-keyed waitlist position lookup with `fetchAccountTrayPoints`, but the React Query key is a constant: `['account-tray', 'accounts-me-points']`. Because the query has a 15 second `staleTime`, React Query may reuse fresh cached data when a different Privy user logs in or opens the tray on the same browser before the cache becomes stale. The fetch itself uses the current user's Privy token, but that token is not represented in the cache key and the cached response is rendered directly into the points module. This can expose the previous local user's point totals, leaderboard rank, eligibility state, and point activity to the next user of the same browser/session. The cache key should include a stable authenticated-user identifier, such as `accountProfile?.privyUserId`, or the query should be explicitly cleared on logout/account changes.

title: Keeper listing accepts mismatched share token bindings
description: Strict CreatorRegistry validation correctly detects when the DB/configured share token differs from `getShareOFTForToken`. This commit now treats `share_token_mismatch` as eligible for the grandfathered fallback, but that fallback only checks that the vault is deployed and that `vault.asset()` equals the creator coin. It does not prove that the supplied `shareTokenAddress` is the registry share token, a deployed share token, or otherwise bound to the vault. As a result, a keeper vault row with a stale, undeployed, or attacker-controlled share token can pass `validateKeeperVaultListing` as `grandfathered_onchain`. The protected `/api/vaults/active` response then returns that untrusted share token, and `/api/keeper/jobs/enqueue-active-vaults` may enqueue automation for the row. This weakens the registry binding used as a safety gate and can cause fee/gating mis-attribution or keeper automation failure for affected vaults.

title: Charm auth helper allows mismatched delegate-only vaults
description: The introduced resolveCharmAutomationAuthorization helper correctly rejects an explicitly mismatched keeper and an explicitly mismatched owner, but its final fallback authorizes any remaining configuration. If manager is not the protocol treasury, delegateAddress is set to an address different from keeperAddress, and charmKeeper/charmOwner are null, execution reaches the final authorized return. This is a regression from the previous direct check, which required delegateAddress == keeperAddress or owner == keeperAddress. In the signal listener this can enqueue Charm rebalance actions for vaults the keeper is not actually authorized to operate; in the rebalance manager it can proceed to a direct rebalance transaction attempt. Onchain Charm authorization should prevent asset loss, so the practical impact is unauthorized queue mutation, failed execution attempts, alert noise, and possible keeper resource/gas waste rather than direct fund compromise.

title: Dev dry-run logs may expose upstream Base RPC secret
description: The commit changes frontend/scripts/dev-deploy-dry-run.sh so BASE_RPC_URL is set to BASE_FORK_UPSTREAM_RPC_URL instead of the local fork URL. BASE_FORK_UPSTREAM_RPC_URL is required by the script and commonly contains provider credentials or API keys in the URL. Later, the startup echo prints BASE_RPC_URL without redaction. Before this commit, that same echo printed only the local fork URL, so provider credentials were not exposed by this log line. This is primarily a local/dev operational secret exposure: an attacker would need access to the developer terminal output, CI/dev logs, or shared troubleshooting logs, but the leak can disclose usable RPC credentials and quota-bearing endpoints.

title: Public metrics requests now run schema ALTERs
description: ensureCreatorMetricsSchema now calls ensureCreatorMetricsStateColumns() and ensureCreatorMetricsConstraints() even when the public creator metrics tables already exist. Those helpers issue ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS and ALTER TABLE ADD CONSTRAINT statements. This function is reached from public read endpoints such as /api/zora/metrics and /api/v1/explore/vaults. On PostgreSQL, ALTER TABLE requires table ownership and takes strong table locks even when the column already exists. In a least-privilege deployment where migrations have already created the columns but the application role does not own the table, these public endpoints will fail on every cold start. If the role does have DDL privileges, bursts of unauthenticated cold-start requests can repeatedly take DDL locks on creator_metrics_state and block normal reads/writes for metrics sync. The safe pattern is to apply these changes only through migrations or an authenticated/admin startup path, or preflight exact missing columns/constraints and avoid DDL from public request handlers.

title: Control-plane writes fail open without audit locks
description: The commit adds control-plane operation persistence and relies on operation rows for lifecycle audit, idempotency, and active-lock constraints. However, the database migration defines operation_kind with a regex that does not allow '.', while the new code uses dotted operation kinds such as vault.settle, vault.provision, operator.action, and solana.reconcile. These inserts violate the check constraint. startControlPlaneOperation catches non-ControlPlaneOperationError database failures, logs them, and returns persisted: false instead of failing closed. settleVault does not check persisted and proceeds to update keepr_vaults and return success. As a result, settlement writes can happen without control_plane_operations, stages, events, idempotency records, or active-lock enforcement. Async verbs may also fail or behave inconsistently because they enqueue jobs with operation_id/stage_id references that were never persisted.

title: /gmeow logs provider auth error text
description: The /gmeow path already suppresses Pinata/OpenClaw provider failure text from the user-facing reply when it looks like an auth/provider error. This commit adds warning logs that include the first 120 characters of that same provider-returned text, and logs raw thrown error messages. The fallback detector explicitly matches strings such as OAuth token refresh failures and OpenClaw logs. If the provider error includes tokens, internal logs, account identifiers, or other operational details, those values are now persisted to application logs via the shared logger, which performs JSON serialization but no secret redaction. This is primarily an information exposure to log storage/observers rather than direct public disclosure, so the severity is low. The safer behavior is to log only structured enums such as fallbackReason/provider and omit or heavily redact provider-originated text and exception messages.

title: XMTP telemetry leaks sender identifiers
description: The new telemetry payloads for `eliza_message_received` and `eliza_message_outcome` include user-identifying XMTP metadata such as `senderAddress`, `senderInboxId`, `conversationId`, `messageId`, and client/source hints. `emitTelemetryEvent` writes the full payload to application logs and optionally POSTs it to `ELIZA_TELEMETRY_WEBHOOK_URL`. Although message content is not included and telemetry is disabled by default, enabling telemetry can disclose private DM relationship metadata and wallet-to-XMTP-inbox linkage to log processors or an external telemetry webhook without redaction or hashing.

title: Production /story page ships iframe screenshot debug hook
description: frontend/public/story/index.html contains a `data-pplx-inline-edit` script that activates whenever the page is loaded in an iframe. It listens for `INLINE_EDIT_CAPTURE_REQUEST` messages without checking `e.origin`, clones and serializes the full document, renders it through an SVG/canvas, and sends a PNG data URL back to `window.parent` using targetOrigin `*`. Because the same page contains a waitlist form with email and optional X handle fields, this becomes a page-content/PII capture primitive if an attacker can frame the page, for example in a deployment missing the configured `frame-ancestors 'self'` CSP or through any same-origin framing gadget. The configured Vercel CSP substantially reduces immediate exploitability in production, but this development hook should not be shipped in a public page.

title: AMOE refund rollout doc uses nonexistent TTL flag
description: The added AMOE rollout plan materially understates the orphan-refund delay for Phase-A `burn-credits` debits. In Phase 2 it states that abandoned burns are picked up after `AMOE_BURN_REFUND_AGE_SEC`, defaulting to 900 seconds, and the rollout/rollback guidance assumes refunds should be observed during a 6-hour soak. The actual refund helper does not read `AMOE_BURN_REFUND_AGE_SEC` at all; it reads `AMOE_REFUND_AGE_EPOCHS`, falls back to `DEFAULT_REFUND_AGE_EPOCHS = 7`, and multiplies by 86,400 seconds. Operators following this document would believe the refund safety net is active within minutes, while abandoned Phase-A debits can remain unreimbursed for about 7 days. This can leave users' AMOE credits economically stuck during rollout or rollback and can cause operators to proceed past Phase 2 without having actually verified refund behavior.

title: User prompts can trigger persistent agent file edits
description: The new Spanish dialect persistence is implemented as an LLM instruction rather than as deterministic host-side code. Any allowed Hermit user whose prompt contains a dialect flag or text hint causes the host prompt to instruct the Pinata agent to use its file edit tool on workspace MEMORY.md before returning JSON. Because the raw user input is appended into the same prompt immediately after these tool-use instructions, an attacker can combine a dialect trigger with prompt-injection text attempting to broaden or alter the file edit. The seeded SOUL/MEMORY files also teach the agent that this write is expected. If the Pinata agent exposes workspace file editing as documented, this allows untrusted chat content to influence persistent shared agent state across later turns/users. The intended safe bullet value is host-derived, but enforcement is delegated to the model instead of a trusted parser/writer, so it is vulnerable to instruction-following failures and prompt injection.

title: Dev loopback redirect can become an open redirect
description: The commit introduced `resolveDisallowedLoopbackRedirectUrl` and wires it into startup for Vite dev builds. The redirect target is constructed with `new URL(current.pathname + current.search + current.hash, configured.origin)`. If the current path starts with a double slash, for example `http://localhost:58492//evil.example/cb?code=secret#token`, `current.pathname` is `//evil.example/cb`; passing that to `new URL(..., configured.origin)` produces `http://evil.example/cb?code=secret#token` rather than a URL on the configured localhost origin. `redirectDisallowedLoopbackPort` then calls `window.location.replace(target)`. This is limited to `import.meta.env.DEV` and loopback origins, so production impact is low, but it can still leak query parameters or fragments from development auth flows and can be abused as a phishing/open-redirect primitive when the app is served through a disallowed loopback proxy port.

title: Enroll endpoint leaks RPC error details to authenticated callers
description: This commit adds a bytecode probe (`isContractAddressByBytecode`) in `/api/arch-b/enroll` and, on failure, returns `err.message` directly in the HTTP response (`parent_csw_probe_failed`). Viem/transport errors commonly include request metadata such as RPC URL and request body.
