Because `getBasePublicClient()` sources the RPC URL from `BASE_RPC_URL`, deployments using provider URLs with embedded credentials can leak sensitive infrastructure details to authenticated users whenever the probe throws (e.g., upstream timeout/rate-limit/outage).

title: Deploy v2 status/resume endpoints lack rate limiting
description: The new deploy session v2 status and resume endpoints do not enforce RATE_LIMITS checks. They accept POST requests, parse the sessionId, and either return status or run the workflow (including up to 25 ticks per request) without any throttling. This allows any authenticated user to repeatedly hit these endpoints and trigger database reads plus workflow invocations, increasing the risk of resource exhaustion or degraded service availability compared to the previous v1 handlers.

title: Gitleaks allowlist masks 0x40-hex secrets globally
description: The commit expands the rule-scoped allowlist for the generic-api-key detector to include `.env.example` templates and a regex that suppresses any `0x` + 40 hex string anywhere in the repo. Because the generic-api-key rule is the fallback detector for non-provider-specific secrets, this means custom API keys or internal tokens that happen to be 20-byte hex (or that are placed in `.env.example`) can bypass CI detection. This is a security regression that could enable accidental or malicious credential leakage.

title: Owner approval debug tags expose paymaster error details
description: The commit adds an owner-approval debug tag that embeds RPC error details (including paymaster debug context) into errors and automatically enables the paymaster debug header whenever an approvalRunId is present. These tags are then extracted and appended to user-facing messages in the onboarding flow. As a result, authenticated users triggering owner approval errors can receive internal paymaster debugging data (store addresses, validation contexts, and raw RPC details) that was previously gated behind PAYMASTER_DEBUG_HEADER_ENABLED. This is an information disclosure risk in production.

title: CSV export script allows spreadsheet formula injection
description: The newly added `exportTopCreators.ts` script selects profile data such as handle, display name, description, and website from `zora_profiles` and serializes them directly to CSV. The `escapeCsv` helper only quotes commas/quotes/newlines and does not neutralize values starting with `=`, `+`, `-`, or `@`. If a malicious creator sets a profile field to a formula (e.g., `=HYPERLINK(...)` or `=IMPORTDATA(...)`), analysts opening the exported CSV could trigger formula execution and data exfiltration or other spreadsheet-based payloads. This is a classic CSV injection issue introduced by the new export script.

title: Stale /api/accounts/me cache can leak prior user CSW
description: The new useAccountMe hook caches /api/accounts/me responses in module-level variables and skips refetching when cached is set. There is no invalidation when the SIWE session changes or on sign-out; the cache is only cleared on window focus or manual refresh. useCanonicalIdentity then trusts accountMe.me.accountSignals.canonicalCswAddress regardless of session state, and components like the /accounts hero render the CSW when identity.cswAddress is non-null. On a shared device, logging out and returning to /accounts (or signing in as a different user without a full reload) can show the previous user's canonical smart wallet and related identity data until focus/refresh, causing a cross-user information leak and identity mix-up.

title: x402 activation nonce never persisted, enabling replay gas drain
description: The migration adds `x402_authorization_nonce` with a unique index to prevent replayed EIP‑3009 authorizations, but the x402 activation handler only passes the nonce inside `metadata` and `insertPendingActivation` ignores the column entirely. As a result, every activation row leaves `x402_authorization_nonce` NULL, so the uniqueness constraint never fires. A malicious user can replay the same signed authorization, and the server will keep calling `settleX402Payment`, causing the relayer to pay gas for reverted `transferWithAuthorization` transactions. This enables a relayer-gas drain / availability issue that should be blocked by persisting and checking the nonce before settlement.

title: Arch B caps bypassed for ERC20 /send transfers
description: The Arch B /keepr send path builds a UserOp and forwards a `valueWei` amount into `submitUserOpOrRefuse`. For ERC20 transfers it explicitly sets `nativeValueWei = 0n`, and the submitter only applies caps and records daily spend when `valueWei > 0n`. As a result, ERC20 (USDC) transfers bypass the new per-profile per‑tx and daily caps entirely. This weakens the mitigation intended to limit wallet spend across vaults; an authorized sender (or compromised issuer) can move ERC20 funds up to the vault-level caps without the Arch B per-profile guardrails.

title: Public referrer lookup enables referral-code enumeration
description: The newly added waitlist referrer handler looks up profiles solely by referral code and returns display/points for any match. Referral codes are derived from email-local parts or other predictable sources, and this endpoint acts as an existence oracle (data vs null) while also exposing points totals even for profiles that are not publicly ranked (no profile_completed_at filter). This weakens privacy by allowing unauthenticated callers to probe for sign‑ups and extract points data that the leaderboard intentionally hides for incomplete profiles.

title: X-Forwarded-For fallback enables IP rate-limit spoofing
description: The commit changes getClientIp() to always fall back to the X-Forwarded-For header in production when edge headers are absent. Because X-Forwarded-For is commonly client-controllable and the code takes the first IP in the list, an attacker can spoof arbitrary IPs (or rotate them) to evade IP-based rate limits across API handlers. The RPC proxy then applies these potentially spoofed IPs to its per-IP limiter (and skips IP limiting when the IP is "unknown"), enabling abuse of rate-limited endpoints such as RPC proxying, auth, and other APIs that rely on getClientIp for throttling. This weakens protections against high-volume abuse and can lead to resource exhaustion or higher upstream costs.

title: Host header injection in social-preview OG metadata
description: The newly added /api/social-preview handler derives the origin from x-forwarded-host/host without an allowlist and uses it to construct og:url and og:image metadata in the HTML response. Because the endpoint sets public cache headers, an attacker can send a request with a spoofed host header and poison cached preview metadata, causing social bots to display attacker-controlled URLs/images (phishing/preview defacement).

title: Wallet noise script unlocks window.ethereum for overrides
description: The added wallet noise bootstrap runs before the app loads and, when it detects a locked Ethereum provider descriptor, replaces it with a configurable/writable property. Wallet providers often lock window.ethereum to prevent other scripts from overriding or proxying the provider. This change removes that safeguard for any page that loads the script. As a result, any subsequent script executing in the page (including third-party scripts) can replace window.ethereum with a malicious provider wrapper that intercepts signing requests, falsifies addresses or chain data, or proxies calls to an attacker-controlled backend. This is a security regression compared to keeping the locked descriptor intact.

title: Swap token selector trusts uncurated API coins as verified
description: The commit adds a swap token discovery path that fetches creator coins from the explore API and unconditionally sets `verified: true` for each returned address. The token selector only triggers the unverified-token confirmation when `verified === false`, so these API-sourced entries bypass the warning entirely. Because the explore endpoint enumerates all vaults in the database (not a curated list), a malicious actor can deploy a scam coin/vault and have it appear as “verified” in the swap UI, increasing the chance users unknowingly trade into an untrusted token.

title: Swap token discovery marks unvetted creator coins as verified
description: The commit adds a new token discovery helper that pulls creator-coin addresses from the public explore/vaults API and marks each returned option with "verified: true". The swap UI uses the "verified" flag to decide whether to show the unverified-token confirmation; therefore any coin that appears in the explore list (which is not a verified/curated registry) is treated as trusted. An attacker can deploy a lookalike creator coin, have it appear in the explore feed, and users will be able to select it without the safety confirmation, increasing phishing/scam risk.

title: Uniswap route allowlist can be bypassed via body.routing
description: The updated Uniswap order and swap handlers derive the routing value from a top-level body field before inspecting the quote object. Because validateRoutePolicy only checks the provided routing candidate and the request body is forwarded unchanged to Uniswap, an attacker can supply an allowed routing value in body.routing while embedding a disallowed route type inside the quote. This bypasses the UNISWAP_ALLOWED_ROUTE_TYPES policy and permits use of route types the operator intended to block.

title: Chat runtime now logs full conversation IDs
description: `generateLlmResponse` now logs `params.groupId` directly in multiple info/warn paths. The previous redaction helper was removed, so Telegram/Discord/web conversation IDs (which can be user- or group-identifying) are written verbatim to log sinks. Anyone with access to centralized logs can correlate or enumerate chats, creating an information disclosure risk.

title: Telegram miniapp link no longer checks shared API secret
description: The commit removes the verifyTelegramLinkApiSecret gate in the Telegram miniapp linking handler. Even when TELEGRAM_LINK_API_SECRET is configured for server-to-server protection, the endpoint now processes requests directly after the POST method check. This means any client that obtains a valid link token (e.g., leaked from the Mini App URL) and has a Privy token can call the endpoint without the shared secret. That weakens defense-in-depth for a sensitive account-linking action and could allow unauthorized linking if tokens are exposed.

title: Unbounded ENS profile cache allows memory DoS via API calls
description: The newly added onchain identity hydration introduces a process-wide Map cache keyed by address. Entries are inserted on every lookup and only gated by a TTL check on read, but expired entries are never removed. The public portfolio endpoint calls this resolver for each request, so an attacker can repeatedly query different addresses and force the cache to grow without bound, eventually exhausting memory and causing a denial of service.

title: Documentation leaks production provisioner host details
description: The updated AGENTS.md documents the live Vultr provisioner host, including its public IP, root SSH command, filesystem paths, and service management commands. Publishing these operational details in a public repo increases the attack surface (targeted scanning, brute force, or social engineering against the provisioner) and exposes internal infrastructure information that should remain private.

title: On-chain owner fallback bypasses DB-linked ownership checks
description: The deploy session ownership verification now falls back to an on-chain `isOwnerAddress` check whenever the profile is missing, the DB is unavailable, or the owner/session address is not linked in the database. This means any address added as an on-chain Coinbase Smart Wallet owner (including unlinked or revoked wallets and temporary/delegated owners) can create deploy sessions even if offchain canonical-wallet linkage fails. Because the allowlist check is satisfied by the smart wallet address, this change enables unlinked on-chain owners to access server-managed deployment sessions and paymaster-backed flows, bypassing the intended DB-based ownership controls.

title: Keepr /ai command now usable without vault configuration
description: The updated keepr command handler processes /ai commands before checking whether the group is configured with a vault. This bypasses the previous gating that limited LLM calls to configured groups. As a result, any group that can reach the bot can invoke generateLlmResponse, consuming server-side LLM API quota/credits and enabling resource abuse without authorization.

title: XMTP commands can abuse OpenClaw API keys without auth
description: The message router now forwards every incoming XMTP message to all plugin actions. The new wallet intelligence actions accept user-supplied addresses and immediately call the OpenClaw execute endpoint (with storage enabled for /intel). OpenClaw in turn invokes server-side portfolio intelligence that relies on paid API keys such as DEBANK_ACCESS_KEY. Because there are no authorization or rate-limit checks in the agent, any XMTP participant can repeatedly trigger these calls, consuming paid API quota and potentially filling Grove/Supabase storage. This is a resource-abuse/availability risk introduced by the new plugins.

title: Future-dated XMTP messages can poison agent checkpoints
description: The commit persists last_processed_message_at based on the maximum observed message timestamp. Because XMTP message timestamps originate from senders and are not constrained here, a malicious member can send a message with a far-future timestamp. The handler stores that timestamp in the database and uses it to filter subsequent message queries, effectively suppressing all future commands until that time elapses (or manual DB intervention). Previously, timestamps were kept only in-memory, so poisoning would reset on cold start; the new persistence makes the DoS durable.

title: Charm factory vaults leave governance under external control
description: Previously, CharmAlphaVaultDeploy was initialized with initializeAndTransfer, which set governance/keeper to the protocol or creator. The refactor now calls Charm’s createVault factory directly and never transfers governance or sets protocol fee/strategy ownership. The factory interface only accepts a manager, so vault governance remains with the external factory (or its governance). This grants a third party the ability to change strategy, adjust protocol fees, or otherwise manipulate vault management, which can impact vault asset safety if that external governance is compromised or malicious.

title: API router allows prototype path to crash handler
description: The newly added root /api/[...path].ts routes user-controlled subpaths directly into the apiRoutes object using bracket lookup. Because apiRoutes is a normal object, prototype properties (e.g., "__proto__", "constructor", "toString") are truthy and bypass the 404 check. The handler then attempts to invoke a non-handler (Object prototype) which throws or never responds. An attacker can send repeated requests to these special paths to force errors/timeouts and waste serverless execution time, creating a low-effort availability attack surface. Use Object.hasOwn(apiRoutes, subpath) or create apiRoutes with Object.create(null) to prevent prototype property lookups.

title: Canonical AlfaClub key routes get stuck on loader
description: RootRouter computes `shouldRouteToAlfaClub` from `resolveAlfaClubCanonicalPath(location.pathname)` and renders `AlfaClubHostRedirect` whenever it is truthy. This commit added `/keys` and `/explore/keys` themselves to `LEGACY_TO_CANONICAL`, while also adding real App routes for those same paths. As a result, app-host visits to `/keys` or `/explore/keys` are intercepted before App can render the intended routes. `AlfaClubHostRedirect` builds an absolute URL on `APP_ORIGIN`; on the canonical app host that URL equals the current page, so `isCurrentWindowUrl(target)` returns without calling `window.location.replace`, leaving the component to render only `AppLoadingRegistrar` indefinitely. This is an availability/functional regression for the key surfaces, not a direct security vulnerability.

title: Finalize uses invalid AccountInfo resize API
description: The commit adds `finalize_pending_entries` to grow a 10 KiB PendingEntries shell into the full 12,352-byte zero-copy account. However, the implementation calls `.resize(target_len)` on an `AccountInfo`. In the Solana program API used by Anchor, account data is resized with `AccountInfo::realloc(new_len, zero_init)`. As written, this new instruction is likely a build-breaking bug, preventing the Solana hook program from being built/upgraded and therefore preventing the intended allocation fix from being deployed.

title: Deployment gas budget now underfunds phase2 UserOps
description: The patched constants force fat deploy-session UserOps to use a 15.9M callGasLimit and 500k verificationGasLimit. The previous code documented phase2 executeBatch as needing roughly 16.4M call gas alone, so lowering the limit below that measured execution requirement can make phase2 self-bundled UserOps run out of gas. Because withDeploySessionUserOpGas overwrites any actual estimate with these constants, callers cannot recover by estimating a higher phase2 call gas value. The handleOps transaction is then sent with the capped gas budget derived from those fields, so the change can cause deployment sessions to fail or become stuck rather than solving the oversized-operation problem. This appears to be an availability/operational regression, not a direct security vulnerability.

title: Activation UserOps rejected by session binding mismatch
description: The commit changes Privy auth so the HttpOnly 4626 session cookie represents the canonical parent CSW when available. The new activation provisioning endpoint, however, signs its activation policy token with `sessionAddress` set to the embedded EOA. During the silent server-owner install, the frontend sends the activation token to `/api/paymaster`; the paymaster reads the authenticated principal from the session cookie and passes that CSW address as `sessionAddress` into `validateActivationOwnerBinding`. That validator requires the token session address to equal the paymaster session address, so normal activation requests fail with `activation_owner_policy_session_mismatch`. The integration between the canonical session model and the activation-owner policy needs to be aligned, e.g. by binding the token to the canonical session principal separately from the embedded owner, or by having the paymaster validate against both expected addresses explicitly.

title: Counter-trade signals misread price ratios as percents
description: The backtest engine stores priceChangePct as a fractional return, e.g. a 3% move is 0.03. The newly exposed counter-trade signal path parses this value and compares it directly against percentage thresholds such as 1.5 and 15, then formats it with a percent sign without multiplying by 100. As a result, a typical 3% move is reported as +0.03% and remains below the 1.5 threshold, so paid signal requests will usually return NEUTRAL instead of long-bias or short-bias. The underlying scale mismatch existed in the signal helper, but this commit makes it externally reachable through VirtualsAcpService.

title: Lean win-chance target uses unscaled USD inputs
description: The new Aristotle/Lean proof target models the win-chance input as whole-dollar values while the Solidity implementation divides a 1e6-scaled USDC/USD amount by 250,000. As written, the Lean prompt asks to prove impossible equalities such as `winChancePPM 1 40000 = 4`, but with the provided definition `min (1 / 250000) 40000` evaluates to 0. The correct whole-dollar examples would need to pass scaled values such as 1,000,000 for $1, or the model must explicitly define a conversion from dollars to 1e6 units. This does not affect deployed code or authentication behavior, but it can cause verification work to fail or create misleading documentation around lottery probability.

title: Vercel env sync fails on newly added aliases
description: The updated sync-v1180-vercel-env.sh script adds several new CREATOR_* and VITE_CREATOR_* environment aliases, but the new hang-workaround in upsert_env only recognizes the Vercel CLI success message for existing variables: "Overrode Environment Variable". When one of the newly introduced aliases does not already exist in Vercel, the CLI normally succeeds with an "Added Environment Variable" message. The script then kills/waits for the process, fails the grep check, prints FAIL, returns 1, and because set -e is enabled, aborts the full sync. This can leave production/development env state partially updated and skip the redeploy and AMOE publish-cron trigger. This is an availability/deployment reliability bug rather than an attacker-exploitable security flaw.

title: Protocol CSW default blocks EOA-only agent startup
description: Before this change, a CSW runtime was considered configured only when the relevant CSW address and Privy wallet env vars were explicitly present, so `XMTP_AGENT_PRIVATE_KEY` could be used as the single-agent fallback. The new validator normalizes `configuredProtocolRaw || PROTOCOL_CSW_ADDRESS`, which means `hasCswAddress` is always true because the policy constant is always present. It then unconditionally requires `PROTOCOL_CSW_PRIVY_WALLET_ID` or the canonical fallback, regardless of whether `XMTP_AGENT_PRIVATE_KEY` is configured. Since startup validation errors lead to `process.exit(1)`, any environment intentionally running the XMTP agent with only an EOA private key will crash during startup and remain offline. This is an availability/configuration regression rather than an externally exploitable security vulnerability.

title: Share-mesh keeper loses legacy batcher fallback
description: The commit renamed deployment-batcher configuration from CREATOR_VAULT_BATCHER to DEPLOYMENT_BATCHER. In `resolveShareMeshCompletionConfig`, the fallback expression was changed from `process.env.DEPLOYMENT_BATCHER ?? process.env.CREATOR_VAULT_BATCHER` to `process.env.DEPLOYMENT_BATCHER ?? process.env.DEPLOYMENT_BATCHER`. This is a no-op fallback and means environments that still have only the legacy key configured resolve `deploymentBatcher` to null. Downstream, `completeShareMeshForSweep` treats a null deployment batcher as `missing_config` and returns before calling `deployShareMeshLpManager`, so keeper share-mesh completion can silently stop after the rename.

title: RPC fallback is not exercised on request failures
description: The commit adds rpcCandidates and createBasePublicClient() to fall back from BASE_RPC_URL to https://mainnet.base.org. However, viem createPublicClient()/http() construction is synchronous and generally does not validate endpoint health or capacity. The helper returns the first candidate immediately, so later readContract calls in resolvePrivyCoinbaseSmartWalletOwnerContext() still fail if the configured Alchemy/Base RPC is over capacity. The EOA path similarly always passes rpcCandidates[0] when BASE_RPC_URL is set, so it also never falls back to the public RPC on runtime failures. This is an operational reliability bug in the newly added fallback behavior, not a security vulnerability.

title: Hook provisioning sends wrong address encoding
description: The commit wires /api/keeper/solana/provision-creator to call the Solana provisioner /setup-creator endpoint. The request body sends `hubCreatorCoin` as `params.creatorToken` and `hubShareToken` as `shareOft`, both normal 20-byte EVM addresses such as `0x` + 40 hex chars. However, the provisioner ultimately invokes `kpr/scripts/solana/deploy/setup-creator-full.ts`, whose `hexToBytes32` helper rejects anything other than `0x` + 64 hex chars. As a result, normal keeper-triggered hook setup will fail with `Invalid bytes32 hex` before initializing the Token-2022 hook mint and PDAs. The fix is to encode/pad the EVM addresses to bytes32 before sending them, or make the provisioner/script accept EVM addresses and left-pad them internally.

title: XMTP reaction history is dropped when loading chats
description: XMTP reactions are represented as structured content, not plain string content. The new decoder branch correctly recognizes `isReaction(msg)` and converts it to a `ChatMessage` with `kind: 'reaction'`. However, `loadMessages()` still filters historical messages to only those whose `content` is a string or that have a fallback before calling `decodedToChat()`. That makes the reaction decoder branch unreachable for historical reaction messages. Live streamed reactions may appear, but they disappear after reloading/reopening the conversation, and the reaction aggregation UI has no reaction rows to count.

title: Production docs source requirement does not fail build
description: The new production build script sets DOCS_REQUIRE_MANUAL_SOURCE=1 before running build:slim. In sync-docs.mjs, that environment variable causes an error to be appended when repo-root manual docs are unavailable and the bundled snapshot fallback is used. However, the script only calls process.exit(1) when --strict is present. build:slim invokes pnpm sync-docs, not sync-docs:strict, so the error is logged but the command can still exit successfully and allow the Docusaurus build to continue with a bundled/stale snapshot. This defeats the intended production guard but does not create a direct security vulnerability.

title: Token rotation docs use ignored AlfaClub env vars
description: This commit rewrote the canonical `docs/operations/alfaclub/token-rotation.md` page and changed the documented Vercel bootstrap variables from the code-supported `ALFACLUB_CHAT_PRIVY_ACCESS_TOKEN` and `ALFACLUB_CHAT_PRIVY_REFRESH_TOKEN` names to `ALFACLUB_PRIVY_ACCESS_TOKEN` and `ALFACLUB_PRIVY_REFRESH_TOKEN`. The runtime refresher still reads only the `ALFACLUB_CHAT_PRIVY_*` variables for env fallback and retry after Privy token rejection. Operators following the new runbook can believe the Vercel fallback has been seeded while the production refresher will treat the access/refresh tokens as missing if the DB row is unavailable, cleared, or stale. The DB seeding path in the runbook can still work, so this is primarily an operational recovery/fallback regression rather than a directly exploitable vulnerability.

title: Undeclared remark dependency can break docs builds
description: The new table-wrapping plugin is wired into Docusaurus via remarkPlugins and imports `visit` from `unist-util-visit`. However, `apps/docs-site/package.json` was not updated to include `unist-util-visit` in dependencies. With pnpm's isolated dependency layout, application source should not rely on transitive dependencies of Docusaurus or MDX packages. A clean install/build can therefore fail with a missing module error before the docs site is generated. This is a documentation-site availability/build reliability bug, not an onchain, API, authentication, or data exposure vulnerability.

title: External EOA fallback can be blocked by wrong session check
description: The new fallback path sets `canonicalSignerAddress` and `canonicalSignerWalletClient` to the connected external EOA when the embedded canonical signer gate is not ready and the external EOA is an on-chain owner of the CSW. However, the `useSwapExecution` call still computes `expectedSessionAddress` as `privyEmbeddedEoaAddress ?? executionSignerAddress` for canonical mode. In fallback cases where `privyEmbeddedEoaAddress` is present but unusable, the actual signer is `executionSignerAddress` (the external EOA), while the session guard expects the Privy embedded EOA. `evaluateCanonicalSubmitSession` rejects if the restored session address differs from this expected address, so the newly added fallback can be unusable unless the session also happens to be for the embedded EOA. This is an availability/correctness bug, not a direct security vulnerability.

title: Waitlist email signup calls auth/privy before bootstrap
description: The active waitlist flow now handles email signup by calling `auth.signIn({ method: 'privy' })` first and only then posting the Privy token to `/api/waitlist/bootstrap`. `useSiweAuth.signIn({ method: 'privy' })` bridges the token through `/api/auth/privy`, which can reject with `RECOVERY_REQUIRED_EMAIL_BOUND` before `/api/waitlist/bootstrap` gets a chance to perform the waitlist/email collision adoption and Privy DID rebind. The legacy pipeline explicitly documented that `/api/waitlist/bootstrap` must run before `/api/auth/privy` for returning users whose email is still bound to an older Privy DID. As a result, legitimate users needing email recovery/rebind can be locked out of the waitlist flow. The same ordering also makes minimal email signup depend on app-session bridging and a ready Privy wallet/session address, rather than letting the waitlist bootstrap complete with the verified email token first.

title: Passive EIP-6963 discovery may break wallet selection
description: The commit removes active dispatch of `eip6963:requestProvider` and leaves EIP-6963 discovery as passive-only. EIP-6963 providers commonly announce during extension initialization and re-announce when a dapp dispatches `eip6963:requestProvider`. Because this app now registers its own listener lazily and also sets wagmi `multiInjectedProviderDiscovery` to false, wallets that already announced before the listener was installed may never be recorded in `eip6963Providers`. Targeted MetaMask/Rabby selection can then fall back to legacy `window.ethereum` inspection or fail to find the intended wallet in collision scenarios. This is a usability/connectivity regression, not an authentication bypass or direct asset-risk vulnerability.

title: Non-security waitlist hook type regression
description: The runtime behavior of the waitlist authentication flow does not appear to introduce an exploitable authentication bypass or security issue. However, the commit creates a TypeScript contract mismatch: privyAuthed was removed from the hook parameter type, but the hook implementation still accesses params?.privyAuthed as an override before falling back to internalPrivy.authenticated. In strict TypeScript this is an additional TS2339-style type error and also makes any intended caller override no longer type-valid.

title: Privy refresh failures masked as cron success
description: The chat token refresh endpoint is cron-secret protected and is supposed to keep AlfaClub chat Privy identity tokens fresh. This commit adds a special case for invalid Privy bootstrap token errors, but returns HTTP 200 even though the response body says success is false and manual token rotation is required. Vercel Cron and many external monitors primarily alert on non-2xx status codes, so this can silently suppress alerts for a permanent authentication/rotation failure. After the current token expires, the chat bridge may lose authentication until an operator notices and rotates credentials manually.

title: Dropped Ethos refresh function leaves pg_cron jobs failing
description: A prior migration schedules two daily pg_cron jobs, daily-ethos-unified-chart-views and daily-ethos-unified-views, both executing SELECT public.refresh_all_ethos_chart_views(). The new retirement migration drops that function as part of removing the Ethos materialized-view layer, but it does not remove those cron jobs first. On databases where the older migration has already run, the cron entries remain and will fail every day when they try to call the now-missing function. This is an operational reliability bug rather than an attacker-exploitable security vulnerability.

title: InvalidWeight reverts are still classified as generic reverts
description: executeVaultRebalanceStrategies() now has an isKnownRebalanceInvalidWeightRejection() helper, but the catch block checks isKnownRebalanceExecutionRevert() first. Common viem ContractFunctionExecutionError instances for a custom-error revert generally include text such as "contract function rebalanceStrategies reverted" or "execution reverted" along with the custom error selector/data. Because the generic condition is evaluated first, the function throws rebalance_strategies_reverted before the newly added InvalidWeight-specific branch can run. This makes the new invalid-weight executor handling ineffective for typical raw contract reverts and causes the API to return keeper_rebalance_reverted instead of keeper_rebalance_invalid_weight.

title: Hot sync handler can hang after early tick rejection
description: The commit wraps the hot-sync work in runTickPromise and waits for either completion or a handler timeout. However, getDbForCron() is called before the inner try/catch, so if it throws, runTickPromise rejects. The timeoutResult promise attaches a catch handler that only clears the timeout and never resolves or rejects. If that rejection happens before handlerTimeoutMs, the timeout is cancelled and the request never sends a response until the hosting platform kills the function. Previously this failure would propagate as an error instead of causing an indefinite in-handler wait.

title: Ethos cron can hang when DB acquisition rejects
description: The commit wraps the Ethos sync work in runTickPromise and waits on a custom Promise that resolves either on success or on a timeout. However, getDbForCron() is awaited before the inner try/catch, so a database acquisition failure can reject runTickPromise. The outer wait promise's catch handler only clears the timeout and never calls resolve or reject. This leaves the HTTP handler awaiting forever until the hosting platform times it out, instead of returning the prior 500/503-style failure response. This is primarily an availability/observability regression for an authenticated cron endpoint.

title: Premium v2 hero clearance result is never composited
description: In the new premium-v2 render flow, `heroLayer` is pushed into the `overlays` array before breakout processing. When a breakout layer exists, the code later assigns `heroLayer = await eraseHeroUnderBreakoutLayer(...)`, but this only rebinds the local variable; it does not update the previously pushed overlay object. The final composite still uses the original, unerased hero buffer at lines 142-145, then draws the breakout on top at line 156. This regresses the intended duplicate hat/face clearance behavior. I did not find evidence that this creates an exploitable security issue, asset loss, authentication bypass, or information leak.

title: Cached CSW owner lookups return stale owner counts
description: findCoinbaseSmartWalletOwnerIndex now checks the in-memory cache and localStorage-persisted owner index before calling ownerCount. If ownerAtIndex still matches the expected owner, it returns the cached or persisted ownerCountSnapshot immediately. This means ownerCount can be stale for the cache TTL and, for persisted localStorage entries, potentially indefinitely if the owner remains at the same index while the wallet owner set changes. The previous implementation read ownerCount first and only trusted cache when the cached count matched, while persisted entries were refreshed to the current count. This appears to be a correctness regression rather than an authentication bypass, because the owner slot itself is still verified before use.

title: Generic swap failures can trigger high-slippage retries
description: The new retry predicate marks errors containing generic strings such as "would fail on-chain", "would revert", or any Universal Router ExecutionFailed selector as retryable. When auto slippage is enabled, the submit loop then refreshes the quote and silently steps to the next slippage ladder value. Because the default auto escalation cap is 30%, an unrelated revert or an adversarially induced stale/failed simulation can cause the client to resubmit a user swap with a much wider minimum-output tolerance than the originally displayed/expected tolerance. On thin creator pools, this can materially increase sandwich/price-manipulation losses without an explicit user confirmation for the higher slippage.

title: Partial digest delivery is permanently skipped
description: sendDailyBriefToCommandRooms now catches per-room send errors, records successful rooms in posted, and returns success as long as at least one room received the digest. runAlfaClubDailyBrief then records dispatch rows only for those successful rooms. However, future non-force runs call hasDailyBriefDispatchForSnapshot, which returns true if any dispatch row exists for that snapshot, independent of room_id. This means a transient failure for one command room during a multi-room send can result in that room missing the daily digest permanently for that snapshot, because the successful room's dispatch row suppresses all later retries.

title: Command reply ledger is not bootstrapped by the bridge
description: The commit adds commandReplyLedger.ts and calls it from executeCommandBatch, but the ledger helpers do not ensure their table exists. Instead, both the SELECT and INSERT paths catch all database errors and fail open. The migration for alfaclub.command_reply_ledger is registered only under ensureAlfaclubDailyBriefSchema, while the chat bridge's normal cold-start path goes through upsertAlfaClubIngestMessages -> ensureAlfaClubVigilanteSchema -> ensureAlfaclubSchema, which does not include this new migration. In environments that rely on the repository's runtime bootstrap rather than an already-applied Supabase migration, the table will not be created before the bridge uses it, so durable command-reply dedupe is silently disabled. This undermines the intended replay-spam fix, but it does not directly expose secrets, bypass authorization, or affect onchain assets.

title: Custom telemetry sample-rate prefix is ignored
description: Before this commit, shouldSampleEvent(tableName, key, rateEnv) used the caller-provided rateEnv prefix to resolve both the table-specific and global sample-rate environment variables. The new implementation delegates to getTelemetrySampleRate(tableName), which always reads TELEMETRY_SAMPLE_RATE_<table> or TELEMETRY_SAMPLE_RATE. As a result, any caller passing a custom prefix such as AUDIT_SAMPLE_RATE would silently be ignored and would instead use the telemetry default/global rate. I did not find current in-repository callers that pass the third argument, so this is not currently security-exploitable in the checked-in code, but it is an introduced functional regression in the exported helper API.

title: Keepr bootstrap masks startup failures
description: The commit changes the Keepr container to start server/agents/eliza/bootstrap.ts. That bootstrap binds a minimal public health server and returns HTTP 200 for /healthz while index.ts is still loading. If the dynamic import of index.ts fails, the catch handler only logs the error and leaves the bootstrap HTTP server running. Because railway.toml uses /healthz as the deployment healthcheck and the deployment has a single replica with restart-on-failure semantics, the process can remain permanently 'healthy' to Railway while the real XMTP/Keepr runtime never starts. This is an availability/operational bug: static import-time failures in the agent will no longer cause a failed process and automatic restart, and the service can silently lose keeper/agent functionality.

title: Migration comments overloaded function without signature
description: PostgreSQL identifies functions by name plus argument types. The repository already creates a 5-argument public.cleanup_log_retention function, and the later extended retention migration creates a separate 17-argument overload rather than replacing the 5-argument function. The new migration updates the 17-argument overload, but then runs COMMENT ON FUNCTION public.cleanup_log_retention without specifying argument types. In PostgreSQL, an unqualified COMMENT ON FUNCTION is ambiguous when overloaded functions exist and can fail with a 'function name is not unique' style error. That can block this migration from applying cleanly, leaving the post-drop cleanup undeployed or the migration history stuck.

title: Deterministic sampling can drop whole telemetry event classes
description: The commit adds deterministic telemetry sampling and applies it before inserting into chat_command_center_events. The sampling key is conversationId, then commandId, then event. Some producers, including ERC-4337 UserOp health telemetry, submit events without conversationId or commandId. Those events are therefore sampled solely by the constant event string. With the recommended chat_command_center_events rate of 0.15-0.30, an event whose hash bucket is above the rate will never be recorded. For example, xmtp_userop_submission_batch hashes to a bucket around 0.616, so setting TELEMETRY_SAMPLE_RATE to 0.30 would drop all UserOp health batches, causing the admin health endpoint to report no data even while clients are submitting it. This is an observability/monitoring bug rather than a direct security vulnerability.

title: Welcome probe mutates ledger before confirming send
description: The script inserts a room_welcome_sent ledger row whenever --send is passed, before it checks whether the room is an allowed Hermit command room or whether AlfaClub bridge credentials are available. If those later checks fail, the script exits after having marked the wallet as welcomed even though no welcome was posted. Conversely, if the wallet was already claimed, the script logs that the claim was skipped but still proceeds to send the welcome message, bypassing the ledger dedupe semantics. This can cause missed future welcomes or duplicate welcome spam during ops testing. This is an operational integrity bug rather than an externally exploitable security issue because running the script requires local execution and production DB/API credentials.

title: Bootstrap /healthz masks failed Hermit startup
description: During bootstrap, /healthz now returns 200 with ok=true while the main Hermit module is still evaluating. If the dynamic import of index.ts fails, the catch block logs the error but intentionally leaves the bootstrap server running. Since railway.hermit.toml uses /healthz as the deployment healthcheck, Railway can consider the service healthy even though startHealthServer() and startRuntime() were never reached. /readyz still reports not-ready, but it is not the configured healthcheck path. This is primarily an availability/operational correctness bug rather than an externally exploitable security vulnerability.

title: Railway watcher Docker build misses source file
description: The commit changes the Dockerfile to `COPY 1659-risk-watcher.ts ./` and updates the README to instruct Railway to use `scripts/ops/1659-risk-watcher` as the Root Directory. However, the watcher source file is committed at `scripts/ops/1659-risk-watcher.ts`, not inside `scripts/ops/1659-risk-watcher/`. With the documented Railway build context, Docker cannot access files outside the context, so the COPY step fails. This is an availability/operations bug for the risk-monitoring worker rather than a direct security vulnerability.

title: Broken keeper risk watcher can start runaway polling
description: The commit adds a risk-monitoring keeper job, but it does not integrate correctly with the existing keeper runner. The enqueue script creates jobs with kind `1659_hype_risk_monitor`, while the runner only claims `internal_api` and `noop` jobs and rejects any other kind before reading the `payload.path`. Therefore these recurring jobs will remain unprocessed. The intended handler is also not present in the catch-all route map, and its relative import points to `frontend/scripts/...` instead of the repository-level `scripts/...`, so adding the route as-is would fail to load. More importantly, the handler imports a script that unconditionally calls `main()` at module load; under an API/keeper import, `process.argv` will not contain `--once`, so the module starts the continuous `while (true)` polling loop in addition to exporting `run1659RiskTick`. If this handler is routed or otherwise imported by a worker, each cold start can spawn repeated Hyperliquid/Base RPC polling and Telegram sends. The handler itself also lacks the keeper API-key checks used by other keeper endpoints, so exposing it would allow unauthenticated callers to trigger this behavior.

title: Non-BaseApp EOA owner install path disabled
description: The new preference logic selects WaitlistModernParentOwnerInstall whenever showParentCswAddOwnerPanel is true and the Base App sub-account panel is not active. That replaces the prior ZoraAddOwnerSigningPanel path. However, WaitlistModernParentOwnerInstall uses useAddUserOpOwnerInstall, whose submit path explicitly looks for a Base App/Coinbase wallet provider and then requires eth_requestAccounts to return the canonical CSW address. Users in a normal browser with a connectable on-chain EOA owner of the CSW can therefore be routed to a flow they cannot complete, instead of the EOA-owner add-owner flow that was previously rendered. This is an availability/onboarding regression, not a security vulnerability.

title: Account setup no longer reloads after Privy login
description: useAccountSetupController now reads Privy state through refs and declares loadMe with an empty dependency array. The initial effect that calls loadMe depends only on loadMe, so it runs once on mount. On a common unauthenticated initial render, loadMe sees privyRef.current.authenticated as false, clears me, and sets loading false. When the user later completes Privy login, loadMe's identity does not change, so the effect does not rerun and no replacement effect keyed on privyAuthed was added. Pages such as AccountsPage rely on the controller to populate me after login; after this regression they can show the signed-in state but never render the account setup workspace until a manual refresh or another explicit loadMe call occurs.

title: server-core dist build leaves missing runtime imports
description: The commit changes @4626/server-core exports/main to ./dist/*.js and adds a build that transpiles only files under packages/server-core/src with bundle:false. Several server-core source files re-export modules from ../../../server/... using .js specifiers, but those targets are actually .ts files outside server-core/src and are not emitted into dist. As a result, a plain Node/Vercel runtime importing @4626/server-core/dist/index.js will follow exports such as ./auth.js and then try to load ../../../server/auth/_shared.js, which is not generated. This is an introduced availability/runtime packaging regression for canonical package consumers. It is not an attacker-triggerable security vulnerability in itself.

title: Stale CSW gas assessment can be reused for a different wallet
description: The updated submit path trusts any existing `fundingAssessment.ok` and skips `refreshFunding()`. At the same time, `refreshFunding()` now returns `null` on read failure without clearing the existing assessment. Because the cached assessment is not tied to the `canonicalCswAddress` or a freshness timestamp, a previously verified funded wallet can leave an `ok` assessment in state. If the canonical CSW changes and the new live balance read times out or fails, the UI can continue to enable submission and the submit preflight can accept the stale funding result for the new wallet. This does not bypass the later wallet-account authorization or on-chain gas accounting, so it is primarily a correctness/UX issue rather than a security vulnerability.

title: Failed UserOps can be reported as confirmed swaps
description: ERC-4337 EntryPoint transactions can have an on-chain transaction receipt status of success while an individual UserOperation inside handleOps failed. The existing ensureUserOperationSucceeded helper correctly checks the UserOp-level success flag. However, the new polling path catches that failure, then calls readOnchainTransactionSucceeded and returns confirmed if the outer transaction receipt status is success. Canonical swap polling uses this result to set the transaction hash, update the swap completion notice, and append swap activity, so a reverted swap can be shown to the user as confirmed.

title: Bytecode store verifier is misconfigured
description: The commit adds `frontend/scripts/ops/verify-bytecode-store-seeded.ts` as the operator check for v1.12.0 bytecode seeding. Its default manifest path is resolved as `../../deployments/...` from `process.cwd()`. The documented invocation uses `pnpm -C frontend`, so the current working directory is `frontend/`; resolving `../../deployments/...` points outside the repository instead of to `../deployments/...`, causing the verifier to fail unless an operator overrides `BYTECODE_MANIFEST` with a corrected path. Separately, the verifier's required/frontend key lists omit `PayoutRouter`, `VaultShareBurnStream`, and `CreatorCoinPolicyController`. Those three code IDs are computed by the deploy UI and are read from `UniversalBytecodeStore` for Phase 2 auxiliary deployment. A verification run could therefore pass while these required bytecodes are missing, leading to deployment failures when the auxiliary batcher/create2 flow tries to use missing store entries.

title: Zora quote helper rejects valid quote responses
description: frontend/server/_lib/zora/zoraTradeQuote.ts calls the external Zora quote endpoint directly. This commit newly treats the external response as if it were an internal `{ success, data }` envelope and throws unless `raw.success` is true or the string "true". Other in-repo callers of the same Zora endpoint accept a successful HTTP response with `call.target`/`call.data`, which indicates the external API payload is expected to be top-level quote data rather than an ApiEnvelope. As a result, `/api/zora/tradeQuote` can return 502 for valid quote responses, breaking the UI Zora trade flow.

title: Public Dune endpoint can exhaust API credits
description: The commit adds a public GET endpoint that uses the server-side DUNE_API_KEY to execute SQL against Dune. The handler performs no authentication and no rate limiting before invoking runDuneSqlRows. The probe path is especially abusable because /api/analytics/dune?probe=1 is marked no-store and calls runDuneSqlRows('SELECT 1 AS ok') on every request. Attackers do not need CORS access to trigger the endpoint; direct HTTP requests are sufficient. Repeated requests can burn paid Dune credits/API quota and tie up Vercel functions while the server polls Dune for up to 30 seconds for probes or 60 seconds for metric queries. The metric cache reduces repeated identical metric calls only after a successful cache fill and only within a single server instance/cache window, so it does not protect the uncached probe and does not replace endpoint-level rate limiting.

title: SBF build checks can miss legacy strings under pipefail
description: The newly added `build-sbf.sh` validates the compiled Solana program by piping `strings "$SO"` into `rg -q`. Because the script enables `pipefail`, `rg -q` may exit immediately after finding a match and close the pipe while `strings` is still writing. In that case `strings` exits with SIGPIPE, causing the whole pipeline to return a non-zero status. This makes the required `relay_entries` presence check fail spuriously, and more importantly can make the legacy `drain_entries`/`flush_fees` absence check evaluate as false even when those strings are present. The result is unreliable deployment validation: stale or unexpected bytecode containing legacy instructions may not be rejected by this guard.

title: Stale explore sparklines bypass cache TTL
description: Before this change, `loadExploreCoinTableContextByAddresses` only exposed DB sparkline values when `sparkline_30d_updated_at` was within the configured TTL. The commit now parses and returns DB sparkline values regardless of `sparkline_30d_updated_at`. Those values are attached to each explore edge as `trend30d`, after which `hydrateExploreSparklinesOnEdges` treats the row as already hydrated if it has at least two values and will not fetch a fresh series. The frontend also seeds its sparkline cache from inline `trend30d`, so it will not request `/api/zora/exploreSparklines` for those rows either. As a result, old DB entries can be served indefinitely on the read path until some separate background precompute job refreshes them. This is a correctness/data freshness bug for market display data, not an authentication, asset-loss, or information-disclosure vulnerability.

title: Subgraph key loaded too late in backfill script
description: The script intends to load frontend/.env and ../.env itself, then run a subgraph-first sparkline backfill. However, ESM static imports are evaluated before main() runs. The new script statically imports precomputeExploreSparklinesForCoins, which imports resolveCoinPriceSparkline, which imports tokenPoolHistorySeries. tokenPoolHistorySeries snapshots THEGRAPH_API_KEY/GRAPH_API_KEY in a module-level const during import. Therefore, when the operator relies on the script's loadEnvFile() behavior rather than exporting THEGRAPH_API_KEY in the shell, hasGraph can later become true but fetchTokenPoolDayCloseSeries still sees an empty module-level key and never calls the subgraph. If no Zora key is configured, batches will attempt coins and refresh none; if a Zora key is configured, the advertised subgraph-first resolution is silently skipped. This is an operational correctness bug, not a security vulnerability.

title: Keeper env loader can crash on supported Node 20
description: This commit introduces kpr/utils/loadKeeperEnv.ts and computes KPR_ROOT with import.meta.dirname. import.meta.dirname was added after the initial Node 20 releases, while kpr/package.json still declares support for node >=20.0.0. On supported Node versions before import.meta.dirname exists, the value is undefined and node:path.resolve(undefined, '..') throws during module evaluation. Because both solana-keeper-orchestrator.ts and preflight-orchestrator.ts import and call this loader, affected deployments can fail to start or fail preflight before any keeper authentication or action gating runs. This is an availability/compatibility bug rather than a remotely exploitable security flaw.

title: Package scripts still reference archived ops files
description: The owner-mutation scripts were moved out of frontend/scripts into archives/owner-mutation-lane, but package.json was not updated. As a result, running pnpm scripts such as tenderly:part1-matrix, csw:link-owner, or csw:owner-link:backfill will look for missing files under frontend/scripts and fail immediately. This is an operational regression rather than a security vulnerability.

title: Metrics exactness ignores explore backfill state
description: This commit adds `explore_backfill_complete` to track whether Explore-derived financial data has been fully backfilled. However, `/api/zora/metrics` computes `exact` from only `backfillComplete && syncStatus === 'idle'`. Because `totals.partial` is derived from `!exact`, deployments with completed on-chain creator indexing but incomplete Explore financial backfill will report `exact: true` and `partial: false` while market cap, 24h volume, and fees are still incomplete. This can mislead the Explore dashboard into presenting partial indexed totals as complete platform-wide totals.

title: Backfill script ignores documented numeric defaults
description: The newly added readIntEnv helper converts an unset environment variable to an empty string and then calls Number(''), which evaluates to 0. Because 0 is finite, the helper returns the clamped minimum rather than the fallback. As a result, running the recommended command without explicit env overrides does not use the documented defaults: chainId becomes 1 instead of 8453, totalLimit becomes 1 instead of 10000, batchSize becomes 50 instead of 500, maxBatches becomes 1 instead of 100, and projectionLimit becomes 100 instead of 50000. This makes the ops catch-up ineffective and may refresh the projection with a much smaller limit than intended, but it is not an exploitable security vulnerability.

title: Self-auth owner probing can skip a valid slot 0
description: The new probe logic unconditionally sets probeStartIndex to 1 whenever skipPasskeyOwnerSlotsInProbe is true. That flag is already passed by the self-funded relay when ownerIndexOverride is not known. If the connected self-auth wallet's valid signing owner is actually at index 0, or if discovery fails to parse/propagate the owner index, this function will never try owner index 0 and will eventually report that the connected wallet is not an onchain owner. Before this commit, the flag was present but unused, so probing always attempted index 0. The safer behavior would be to skip slot 0 only after verifying ownerAtIndex(0) is the expected unusable WebAuthn/passkey slot, or to fall back to probing index 0 if the later slots fail.

title: Non-security explore loader rendering regression
description: The new ExploreTableLoadingOverlay renders PixelWaveLoader with size="sm". PixelWaveLoader accepts arbitrary strings as CSS size values and assigns them directly to inline width and height. Since "sm" is not a valid CSS length, the browser will ignore the width/height declarations, and the loader may render at zero or otherwise incorrectly. This affects loading-state presentation only; it does not expose data, bypass authentication, alter onchain behavior, or create an exploitable security condition.

title: Legacy Safari can break mobile scroll-story initialization
description: The immersive marketing page now stores the mobile media query in a MediaQueryList and registers a change handler with mobileMq.addEventListener('change', ...). MediaQueryList.addEventListener is not available in some older mobile Safari/iOS WebKit versions, where the legacy addListener API is used instead. In those browsers, this line throws, the current script stops, and the final update() call is not reached. This can leave the scroll-story section uninitialized or hidden until other events happen. The impact is limited to a UI/availability regression on the public marketing page and does not affect authentication, secrets, API behavior, or onchain assets.

title: Shared trust nav drops Risks link from updated pages
description: The changed pages previously had hardcoded primary navigation entries that included /risks. This commit replaces those static links with an empty nav populated by /trust-nav.js. The shared NAV_LINKS array does not include a Risks entry, so the affected pages lose the primary-header link to the risk disclosure page. This is not an authentication, data exposure, XSS, or fund-safety issue, but it is a trust/disclosure UX regression on public legal/trust pages.

title: Chat menu clicks also minimize desktop chat
description: In ChatWindow, the header menu container was changed from stopping click propagation to stopping only mouse down and key down events. At the same time, the desktop header wrapper was changed into a button whose onClick calls onMinimize. HeaderMenuItem buttons do not stop event propagation. As a result, clicking menu items such as View profile, Copy address, or View on Basescan runs the menu action and then bubbles to the outer header button, toggling/minimizing the chat unexpectedly. The new outer button also contains nested buttons, which is invalid interactive markup and can cause inconsistent browser behavior. This is a functional/UI bug, not a security vulnerability.

title: New frontend test violates placement guard
description: The newly added smoke test is located at frontend/src/components/explore/MetricChartPlot.test.tsx. The existing guard:test-file-placement script treats newly added *.test.* files outside src/features/**, src/pages/**, and api/__tests__/** as violations. Running the guard against this commit with TEST_PLACEMENT_BASE=HEAD^ reports this file as disallowed. This is a CI/developer workflow regression, not a runtime or security vulnerability.

title: Cron masks enrichment failures as success
description: After a successful Zora explore scan, the commit wraps wallet enrichment and CSW index reconciliation in a separate catch block. That catch records phase:'enrich_failed' in the internal refresh-state table, but then returns an ok:true, tick:'refreshed' response with no error field. The public cron handler only emits a warning when result.ok is false; otherwise it logs the run as a normal refresh. As a result, failures in linked-wallet enrichment or CSW index reconciliation can persist silently, leaving wallet and is_in_csw_index metadata stale while operational monitoring sees a successful cron tick. This is a reliability/data-integrity bug, not a security vulnerability.

title: Telegram @handle relay sources never match incoming chats
description: The relay configuration parser accepts public Telegram references and converts them to strings like `@groupname`. However, the webhook normalizes incoming updates using only `message.chat.id`, which Telegram supplies as a numeric chat id. The relay matcher then performs an exact string comparison between the numeric incoming id and the configured `@handle`. As a result, any operator using the newly documented @handle or public t.me URL support will silently get no relay and no early return to skip local Telegram command handling. Numeric chat ids and private `t.me/c/...` URLs are not affected.

title: Ethos filter is applied after pagination
description: For non-ETHOS_SCORE creator lists, the handler fetches a single paginated page from the Zora SDK using count/after, resolves Ethos scores for only those returned edges, and then filters that page in memory by ethosMin. Because the threshold is not applied before pagination, excluded low-score rows still consume page slots. A request for a high threshold can therefore return fewer than count rows, or even zero rows, while matching creators exist on later pages. The returned pageInfo also remains the SDK's unfiltered pagination metadata, so API consumers and the UI can show misleading empty or partial results. This was introduced when the frontend began sending ethosMin for all sorts rather than only ETHOS_SCORE, together with the new server-side post-filter.

title: Unbounded Twitter media fetch enables SSRF and DoS
description: The commit adds `downloadTweetMedia`, which accepts a caller-provided media URL if it merely starts with `https://`, then calls `fetch(url)` with default redirect handling and no abort signal. It reads the entire response with `arrayBuffer()` before enforcing any content-type checks and does not enforce `Content-Length` or post-read byte limits. Because `fetch` follows redirects by default, an attacker-controlled HTTPS URL can redirect the server to internal HTTP/HTTPS endpoints. Separately, a large or slow response can consume memory or hold a serverless function until timeout. The code also lets the caller override the response content type via `input.contentType`, weakening MIME validation. This is reachable whenever the new exported `postTweetFromSystem` media parameter is used with untrusted or LLM/user-influenced URLs.

title: Tamago ERC4626 writes deposit state after token call
description: In the added Tamago ERC4626 source, deposit() and mint() compute the receiver balance, total supply, and managed asset updates, then perform safeTransferFrom() on the underlying asset, and only after that write balances, tokenSupply, and managedAssets. Because the external token call occurs before effects are committed and there is no reentrancy guard, a reentrant asset can call back into withdraw() or redeem() during safeTransferFrom(). Those functions can burn shares and reduce managedAssets, but when the outer deposit()/mint() resumes it writes the stale pre-callback balance/supply/asset snapshots plus the new deposit values, potentially resurrecting burned shares and restoring accounting while assets have already been withdrawn. I found no production imports of the Tamago deployer outside the new Tamago tests, so the immediate production impact appears limited; the issue becomes exploitable if this reference module is used as an actual vault with a non-standard/reentrant asset.

title: Hermit now swallows fatal process exceptions
description: The new `unhandledRejection` and `uncaughtException` handlers in the Hermit runtime only update `state.lastError` and log a warning. They do not stop the bridge, close resources, mark readiness unhealthy, or exit for supervisor restart. In Node.js, continuing after `uncaughtException` is unsafe because the process may be in an undefined or partially failed state. The existing `/readyz` response is based only on `state.bridgeStarted`, so a fatal exception can be swallowed while the service still reports ready. This is primarily an availability/reliability issue for the long-lived chat bridge rather than a direct authentication, asset-loss, or data-exposure vulnerability.

title: Swap auto-reconnect bypasses provider-collision guard
description: Swap still detects provider-collision states where injected connectors should be disabled, and the manual wallet picker continues to filter those connectors. However, the automatic recovery effect changed to call selectPreferredWalletConnector(wagmiConnectors) directly. Because selectPreferredWalletConnector can choose MetaMask or a generic injected connector, the page can now auto-reconnect through a connector that the collision guard intentionally hides when multiple injected providers or a locked window.ethereum are detected. In those collision states, a competing or malicious injected provider can be selected before the user explicitly chooses a safe connector, potentially causing signatures or transactions to be requested through the wrong wallet/provider.

title: Stale websocket events poison reconnect backoff
description: The commit introduces exponential websocket reconnect backoff for AlfaClub live sockets. However, the close and error handlers call applySocketBackoff() before checking whether the event came from the socket currently stored in bridgeState.liveSocket. Since ensureLiveCommandSocket() can intentionally close an old socket before replacing it, delayed close/error events from that stale socket can still increase the global backoff state and persist misleading health data. This can suppress later live-socket reconnect attempts for up to the 60 second cap even though the current socket did not fail. The fix would be to move the stale-socket check before applySocketBackoff()/warnWsError, or distinguish intentional closes from network failures.

title: EOA-owner lane rejects real personal_sign signatures
description: The new _submitOwnerViaPreparedCallsWithEoaOwner flow is intended to let an on-chain EOA owner sign a Coinbase Smart Wallet userOpHash directly. However, it calls the signer connector with personal_sign and then validates the returned signature using recoverAddress({ hash: userOpHash, signature }). The personal_sign RPC method signs the EIP-191 Ethereum Signed Message digest, not the raw 32-byte hash. Therefore a compliant MetaMask/Rabby/WalletConnect-style connector will return a signature that recovers to the owner only with recoverMessageAddress/hashMessage, while the current raw recovery check will recover a different address and throw. The tests mock personal_sign by returning a raw digest signature, so they do not catch this real-wallet behavior. This appears to introduce an availability/functional bug in the newly added recovery lane rather than a direct security vulnerability.

title: Skip-vanity flag exports ignored zero CREATE2 salts
description: The commit adds a skip-vanity path to script/deploy-base-full-release.sh that exports every INFRA_*_SALT as 0x00. However, script/DeployBaseMainnetDeployer.s.sol resolves salts by reading the raw salt env var with a default of bytes32(0), and only returns the raw salt if it is nonzero. Therefore a deliberately exported zero salt is indistinguishable from an unset env var and is ignored. The deployment then falls back to INFRA_*_SALT_TAG or the epoch-derived default tag. This breaks the advertised skip-vanity behavior and can cause operators to deploy with unexpected deterministic addresses, or with stale pre-exported *_SALT_TAG values if present. I did not find evidence that this creates a direct attacker-exploitable security vulnerability; it is an operational deployment correctness bug.

title: Hermit setup falsely confirms unsaved preferences
description: The new personalization commands set their local saved flag to true whenever persistPreference resolves without throwing. However, the AlfaClub persistence helper upsertUserPreference is explicitly best-effort and returns false for normal failure modes such as disabled persistence, no DB connection, validation failure, or query errors. The execute.ts wrapper discards that boolean and resolves successfully, so /hermit lang and /hermit tone will tell the user the preference was saved even though no row was written. This can cause confusing behavior: the preference is not applied on future requests, /hermit prefs may show no saved value, and onboarding state may not be persisted. This is not a security issue, but it is an introduced correctness bug in the setup flow.

title: Rotated Privy token write failures are hidden
description: The new default writeBundle only writes access/refresh tokens when they differ from inbound values, which is reasonable for unchanged tokens. However, when Privy does rotate either credential and the corresponding DB upsert fails, the code now only logs a warning and still persists the new identity token. runAlfaClubPrivyRefreshOnce then returns status:"refreshed". This creates an inconsistent credential set: the chat bridge uses the fresh identity token, but the next refresh will read the stale access/refresh token pair from storage. Since the file documents that Privy rejects expired access tokens, this can break future refreshes after the stale access token expires, while the cron endpoint initially returns 200 and monitoring may not detect the real persistence failure.

title: Deleted Groth16 verifier breaks stale CI check
description: The production Solidity references have migrated to the PLONK verifier and I did not find an exploitable on-chain security issue from the deletion itself. However, the repository still contains tools/ci/check_amoe_vk.sh, which is documented as a CI/pre-build guard and unconditionally checks for contracts/utilities/lottery/zk/AmoeGroth16Verifier.sol. Since this commit deletes that file, running the script now fails immediately with '[check_amoe_vk] ... missing'. This can break manual or downstream CI/release workflows that still call the guard.

title: Regression: /hermitimg removed instead of aliased to /meme
description: In executeHermitCommand, the image path condition was changed from `/hermitimg` to `/meme`, so `/hermitimg` is no longer handled and now falls through to the unsupported-command error. The returned `kind` was also changed from `hermitimg` to `meme`, and both server/client type guards were updated accordingly. This is a backward-compatibility break (command and response schema) that can cause existing integrations/clients using `/hermitimg` or expecting `kind: 'hermitimg'` to fail.

title: Drand relay submission path is hard-disabled at runtime
description: In `DrandClient.buildSubmission`, after a basic G1 decompression sanity check, execution unconditionally throws `g1EIP2537EncodeUnsupported` and never constructs calldata payload fields. Separately, `DrandPairingPrecheck.verify` now unconditionally throws `upstreamUnsupported` instead of performing verification. As a result, runtime callers cannot successfully produce drand submissions. The CLI loop catches these errors and continues polling, resulting in a silent/permanent operational failure mode (no round submissions).

title: ReferenceError in new decision panel breaks chart rendering
description: A new function (`renderDecisionPanel`) was added and is called during every `render()` execution. Inside it, comparisons and delta math reference `bcBuyCost`, which is never defined. The defined variable is `bcBuyCoin`. When the function executes under normal defaults, JavaScript throws `ReferenceError: bcBuyCost is not defined`, which breaks the render flow and causes functional denial-of-service of the simulator UI logic.

title: Unescaped Zora token symbol enables DOM XSS in chart doc
description: The new chart logic fetches token metadata from Zora and sets the coin symbol directly from the response. That symbol is then interpolated into HTML and SVG strings that are assigned via innerHTML. Because token symbols are attacker-controlled on-chain metadata, a malicious symbol (e.g., containing HTML/JS) can break out of the markup and execute script when a user refetches the price. This introduces a DOM-based XSS issue in the documentation page.

title: Deploy submissions can be blocked after runtime version updates
description: DeployVaultBatcher’s submit flow fetches the latest runtime config and compares it to a client value to detect stale config. The commit swaps the comparison to use deploymentVersionProp (the build-time/query value) instead of the current deploymentVersion that includes overrides. When the backend bumps deploymentVersion, the mismatch condition remains true on every submit because deploymentVersionProp never updates, so the handler keeps returning early with a “deploy runtime changed” error even after setDeploymentVersionOverride is applied. This effectively blocks deploys until a full frontend redeploy or a URL override, which is a regression from the previous behavior where a single retry would proceed.

title: Outreach CSV export allows spreadsheet formula injection
description: The new indexer export script collects user-controlled profile fields (Zora/Farcaster handles, display names, ENS/Basename names, etc.) and writes them directly into a CSV file. The `escapeCsv` helper only performs RFC4180 quoting for commas/quotes/newlines and does not neutralize leading formula characters (`=`, `+`, `-`, `@`). As a result, a malicious handle or name stored in the database can produce a CSV cell that spreadsheet software interprets as a formula, potentially exfiltrating data or running commands when an operator opens the outreach file. Because the script is explicitly intended for outreach spreadsheet import, this is a realistic vector for CSV injection.

title: Swap canonical session auto-refresh now only runs once
description: The commit replaces the previous attempt-key logic with a simple boolean ref. Once `canonicalSessionAutoRefreshAttemptedRef` is set to true, it is never reset even after a successful refresh or a later account/session change. This means if the first auto-refresh fails (network hiccup) or the user later switches accounts / the session expires again, the page will refuse to auto-refresh and the swap flow can remain stuck until a manual reload.

title: Readiness probe can report ready with zero running agents
description: The commit changes the readiness logic to only require XMTP readiness when agentCount > 0, removing the previous requirement that at least one agent exists when XMTP is required. As a result, if the runtime boots with zero agents (or all agents fail to start), the /readyz probe can still return ready=true even though readinessReasons includes "no_agents". This can mislead monitoring or routing systems into treating the service as healthy while it cannot process work, leading to silent operational outages.

title: Telegram DM send failures are no longer detected by callers
description: The commit wraps sendTelegramMessage in a try/catch and returns {messageId:null} on failures after logging. This prevents the promise from rejecting. Existing logic in the holder-room join flow uses .then(() => true).catch(() => false) to detect if a DM invite was delivered. Because sendTelegramMessage no longer throws, that check now always returns true, so the webhook reports “invite sent via private DM” even when delivery failed. Users can be left without a usable invite and no fallback instructions.

title: Vault deploy predictions ignore ShareOFT salt override
description: In the Telegram vault deploy helper, `predictDeployAddresses` derives the ShareOFT create2 salt solely from owner/share symbol. The AKITA template includes a non-zero `shareOftSaltOverride`, and phase 1 deployments are executed with that override. Because the prediction ignores the override, the ShareOFT address used in phase 2/4 parameters can diverge from the actual ShareOFT deployed in phase 1, causing phase 2 to revert (Phase1Missing) or wiring to an incorrect ShareOFT address. This breaks the deploy-session flow and can misconfigure vault wiring.
